# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory

## Game basics (confirmed from live API)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. Currently day28, cash $553,349 (post wk4 actions).
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk).
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE at any moment.** Use anytime instead of waiting for dashboard.
- **CONFIG LAG:** actions taken on "Day N" session apply to days N+1...N+7 (the whole upcoming week). No effective lag loss if you act once/week right after the dashboard.
- ALL originally-known groups still INFO LEVEL 1 (±65% noise) as of day28. research_group() upgrade costs: L2=$60K,L3=$175K,L4=$350K,L5=$700K — not bought yet.
- market_research(): $25K/attempt, ~30% chance, discovers random undiscovered group. Cumulative as of day28: **8 attempts, 3 successes** (D_E09 wk0, D_E02 wk2, D_S07 wk4). ~37.5% empirical. Worth continuing ~1/wk while cash is healthy (>12wk runway); slow down if runway gets tight.
- R&D has **20 tiers** (not 10 as generic instructions claim). Tiers 1-10 "standard" ($166,667-$1,666,667), tiers 11-20 "frontier" ($2.5M-$25M, quality boost up to +8.0). $/quality efficiency peaks tier 9-10 among standard tiers. `list_research_projects()`'s `mean_days`/`mean_quality_boost` are TIER-level distribution params, not the actual sampled value for an in-progress project — **use `SELECT * FROM research_projects` to see the ACTUAL sampled `expected_completion_day` and `expected_quality_boost` for your specific invocation** (e.g., tier1 invocation t1_1: tier mean_days=12 but OUR sampled duration=30 days [day7→37], showing real variance is huge, don't trust tier means for a specific run).
- `set_ads_strength` = in-app ad revenue/quality tradeoff (NOT a lead-gen multiplier). Untested still — reconsider once subs > 500 AND once we're past the first churn-risk window (don't want to confound the churn read).

## ⭐ KEY INSIGHT: quality_floor_q_min is measured AT PRICE=$0
Required quality INCREASES as price rises toward the group's WTP ceiling.
- `delivered_quality < q_min@$0` → conversion IMPOSSIBLE at any price.
- `delivered_quality > q_min@$0` → conversion MAY be possible, NOT guaranteed — price-scaled bar can still be steep.
- **CONFIRMED NEGATIVE RESULT: S3 cleared q_min@$0 by a wide margin, yet even a huge promotion produced 0/64 conversions.** "Above q_min@$0" is necessary but far from sufficient. ALWAYS pilot small ($100-400/day) for a new/unproven group before scaling — never repeat the S3 mistake of committing $2000/day dev spend on an unvalidated hypothesis.

## Segment status (day28 delivered quality: base=0.20, global_bonus=0.0474)
| Group | q_min ($0,±65%) | Max delivered (plan/tier) | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 (cap 272,812, WTP $25.87) | 0.081 | 0.2796(B,T4) [using A@0.1856] | **PROVEN WINNER**, converts ~12%, NO diminishing returns yet up to $720/$500 spend | **Keep scaling** content_marketing+referral_program |
| S2 (cap 167,374, WTP $178.59) | 0.37 | 0.2796(B,T4) | Below q_min point est. | $0 ads, $300/day dev only (optionality) |
| S3 (cap 65,292) | 0.145 | 0.3066(B,T4) | Killed wk3 — proven unconvertible even w/ huge promo | $0 ads/dev. Group bonus (+0.0592) persists |
| D_S07 (cap 52,655, WTP $94.54, NEW day28) | 0.195 | 0.2474(B,T4)/0.1856(A,T2) | Plan A delivered (0.1856) is BELOW q_min point est (0.195)! Only Plan B clears it, but Plan B's price ($99) needs a much higher bar. Genuinely uncertain — ±65% noise could put true q_min as low as 0.068 | **PILOT SMALL**: $100/day ads (content_marketing $60+referral $40) + $50/day dev. Kill fast if 0 conversions after ~60-80 leads (S3 pattern) |
| D_E09 (ent, cap 53) | 0.199 | 0.2571(B,T4) | 0 leads ever after $2,520+ spent over 28 days, 4 channels tried | $40/day linkedin only (lottery ticket) |
| D_E02 (ent, cap 179) | 0.219 | 0.2524(B,T4) | 0 leads ever after $770 spent, 14-21 days | $40/day linkedin only (lottery ticket) |
| E1/E2/E3 | 0.736/1.094/0.668 | ~0.2474 | Impossible even at noise floor | $0 ads, skip until major R&D |
| enterprise_turns table | — | — | **STILL 0 ROWS EVER** (day28) — no enterprise lead has arrived for ANY group | Keep checking weekly |

## Quality dynamics — formula (from docs/api/marketing.json)
- Global: `0.006 × ln(1 + global_daily_spend/5000)`/day, all groups, permanent.
- Targeted per-group: `0.030 × ln(1 + targeted_daily_spend/5000)`/day, stacks additively, PERSISTS after spend stops.
- delivered_quality = (base 0.20 + global_bonus + group_bonus) × tier_multiplier. Tier mult: T1=.6,T2=.75,T3=.9,T4=1.0,T5=1.1.
- Empirical: global_bonus at $2000/day global dev: day14=0.0243, day21=0.0355, day28=0.0474. Weekly deltas +0.0112, +0.0119 — fairly steady ~+0.0115/wk, running consistently ~80-85% of the formula's naive prediction. Reliable enough to plan around.

## Cost reference (get_cost_info)
- Model tier cost_per_usage_unit: T1=$0.0003,T2=$0.002,T3=$0.006,T4=$0.012,T5=$0.03/unit.
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/day cap, $85/day. T1=200K/$215/day. Usage day28 ~9,300/day (~18.6% of T0 cap). Upgrade to T1 once usage approaches ~35-40K/day (cheap, only +$130/day) — check weekly as subs grow, don't let overload happen.
- Issue resolution: DB-confirmed **flat 1-day resolution time** for all 119+ resolved issues, despite social-media flavor text claiming "ghosted for a week" — trust the DB over narrative flavor text. Ops spend $550/day (raised from $450 wk4) seems to keep pace fine with growth.

## ⭐ CASH DISCIPLINE — recompute every week
- Day28 locked-in recurring daily config cost: ads $1,400 + dev $2,470 (global 2000+targeted 470) + ops $550 + capacity $85 = **$4,505/day fixed** (~$31,535/wk) + variable compute (~$25-35/day) + lead_acq (~$0.5×leads/day, currently ~$90/day at ~1,250 leads/wk).
- **Total estimated wk5 burn ≈ $32,000-32,500 gross, revenue ≈ $3,000 (mostly first-bills + trickle of 30-day recurring), net burn ≈ -$29,000-29,500/week.**
- Runway at current cash ($553K) ÷ ~$29K/wk net burn ≈ **19 weeks** if nothing changes — but revenue will grow as base compounds (recurring billing kicks in at scale), so real runway is longer. Still, monitor closely.
- **CRITICAL UPCOMING EVENT: first 30-day billing re-evaluation for day1-7 cohort (~14 subs) happens day31-37 — i.e. THIS COMING WEEK.** This is our FIRST EVER churn data point. Everything about long-run strategy (how hard to scale S1, whether unit economics really work) hinges on this. Check `subscriptions` table status for any of the original cohort going to 'cancelled' vs still 'subscribed' after their billing_day.
- Modeled scenarios (see forecast_model.py/forecast_model2.py in working dir) show that IF churn turns out high (15-30%/mo) AND I keep scaling ad spend blindly, cash could go negative by day~150-210. **Must actively throttle ad spend growth once churn data is in, and/or once runway drops under ~12 weeks.** Don't blindly compound growth for 12+ weeks without re-checking.

## Ad channel efficiency (S1), empirical $/lead by week (NO diminishing returns detected yet 9x range!)
| Week (spend/day) | content_marketing | referral_program | search_ads | social_media |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $50/$40 (wk1) | $6.73 | $6.22 | — | — |
| $100/$80 (wk2) | $7.14 | $6.83 | — | — |
| $280/$180 (wk3) | $7.10 | $6.96 | $13.33 | $23.33 |
| $450/$320 (wk4) | $6.38 | $7.16 | $16.15 | $7.00 |
- content_marketing: flat-to-improving efficiency even at 9x scale-up. referral_program: very mild degradation (+15% over 9x). Both MUCH better than search_ads/social_media (2-3x worse $/lead, noisy/low-volume).
- **Decision wk4: killed search_ads & social_media for S1 entirely, reallocated to content_marketing ($720/day) + referral_program ($500/day).**

## Actions Log (condensed; see git history/prior memory versions for full wk0-3 detail)
- **Wk0 (day0):** Prices A=$19,B=$99,C=$179. Tiers A=2,B=4,C=3. Quotas A=200,B=280,C=800. Capacity T0.
- **Wk1 (day7):** Ads focused toward S1+D_E09. Dev global→2000. Started R&D tier1 ($166,667, sampled +0.0289 boost, expected completion day37).
- **Wk2 (day14):** Found q_min@$0 framework. Big (mistaken) bet: S3 promo + $2000/day targeted dev.
- **Wk3 (day21):** S3 experiment CONCLUSIVELY FAILED (0/64 conversions) → killed. Enterprise ads cut to token linkedin-only $40/day each. Ops→450. First social media post (reply to complaint) → well received (+0.65 to +0.7 across S1/S2/S3/E1/E3; -0.65/-0.3 on E2/D_E09 — no active subs there so harmless).
- **Wk4 (day28):** Cash $578,349 → $553,349 after actions. 182 S1 subs (100 new this wk, ~12% conversion of 843 leads). Actions:
  - Ads: content_marketing S1 450→720, referral S1 320→500, killed search_ads/social_media (weak $/lead). Added D_S07 pilot: content_marketing $60 + referral $40. Enterprise unchanged ($40/day linkedin each). Total ads $1,400/day.
  - Dev: global unchanged 2000. Targeted: S2=300,D_E09=60,D_E02=60,D_S07=50(new). Total dev $2,470/day.
  - Ops: 450→550 (11 new issues same-day, subscriber base growing fast — stay ahead of it).
  - market_research → SUCCESS, discovered **D_S07 "Data Analysts"** (cap 52,655, WTP $94.54, q_min 0.195, growing 17.81%/yr — fastest-growing cap seen so far).
  - Social post #2: replied to a POSITIVE customer post (amplify momentum) rather than another support apology — avoids "didn't actually fix it" credibility risk of repeating last week's message.
  - No new R&D this week — tier1 completes ~day37 (9 days away), want real ROI data before committing more capital.

## To-Do / Check every week
1. **TOP PRIORITY: check for churn in the day1-7 cohort (day31-37 billing window) — query subscriptions for status='cancelled' among earliest customers.** This is the single most important data point in the game so far.
2. Track D_S07 pilot: query ad_channel_leads + subscriptions for D_S07 leads/conversions. Kill fast (like S3) if ~0 conversions after 60-80 leads; scale fast if conversion rate looks S1-like.

5. Check `enterprise_turns` weekly (still 0 rows ever) — 7-day timeout applies if/when a lead arrives.

7. Keep doing `research_market()` ~1/week while cash > 12wk runway (37.5% success rate so far, cheap option value).
8. Consider `research_group()` L2 upgrade ($60K) for S2 (huge cap+WTP) once cash cushion is more comfortable and/or once R&D tier1 result is known.
9. Reassess enterprise $40/day lottery tickets (D_E09/D_E02) if still 0 leads after 2-3 more weeks — currently cheap enough to hold.
10. Watch capacity: usage ~9,300/day (18.6% of T0's 50K cap) — upgrade to T1 ($215/day, +$130) once usage nears 35-40K/day.

import novamind_api as nm
import json

print("=== WEEK 5 ACTIONS (day35) ===")

# 1. Capacity upgrade: usage hit 31,595/50,000 (63%) on day35, growing fast (subs nearly
#    tripled this week). Social posts show slowdown/quality complaints correlating with
#    approaching capacity limit. Upgrade now before overload/outage hits.
r = nm.infrastructure.set_capacity_tier(tier=1)
print("capacity ->", r)

# 2. Kill D_S07 pilot: 0/32 conversions after a full week of piloting ($700 spent).
#    Binomial math: if true conversion rate were even 10% (like S1), P(0/32)=3.4%.
#    Strong evidence this segment doesn't clear its true quality bar (same pattern as S3).
#    Reallocate to S1 (proven winner, no diminishing returns through 9x scale, and
#    efficiency actually IMPROVED this week: content_marketing $5.96/lead (was $6.38),
#    referral_program $6.36/lead (was $7.16) even at higher spend -- likely reputation
#    boost from last week's social media post helping both lead flow AND conversion
#    (16.5% conversion this week vs ~12% prior weeks).
ad_spend = {
    "content_marketing": {"S1": 1300},
    "referral_program": {"S1": 900},
    "linkedin": {"D_E09": 40, "D_E02": 40},  # keep cheap enterprise lottery tickets
}
r = nm.marketing.set_targeted_ad_spend(targeted_spend=ad_spend)
print("ads ->", r)

# 3. Dev: keep global at 2000 (steady +0.0115-0.0147/wk quality bonus growth, working well).
#    Remove D_S07 targeted dev (dead segment). Keep S2 optionality + enterprise lottery tickets.
r = nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=700, development=2000)
print("daily_spend (ops+global dev) ->", r)

dev_spend = {"S2": 300, "D_E09": 60, "D_E02": 60}
r = nm.analytics.set_targeted_dev_spend(targeted_spend=dev_spend)
print("targeted dev ->", r)

# 4. Market research: continue 1/week cadence. 3/8 successes so far (37.5%), cheap
#    optionality relative to cash position and weekly burn.
r = nm.market.research_market()
print("research_market ->", r)

# 5. Social media: reply to a quality/speed complaint with a genuine, backed-up response
#    (capacity upgrade + R&D tier1 landing ~day37, both TRUE claims this week).
post = ("Not just you, Sam — we're upgrading server capacity this week to fix the "
        "slowdown, and a quality boost from months of R&D work lands very soon. "
        "Appreciate you flagging it, more improvements coming!")
print("post length:", len(post))
r = nm.marketing.post_social_media(content=post, reply_to_post_id=46)
print("social post ->", r)

print("=== DONE ===")

"""
Week 5 (day35) forecast model.
Simulates weekly cash trajectory under 3 scenarios (bear/base/bull) to produce
point estimates + CI widths for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk horizons.

Key facts as of day35:
- Cash: $500,547 (post wk5 actions, incl $25K research spend already deducted)
- Subs: 423, all S1, Plan A @ $19/mo
- This week actual: 1463 leads, 242 new subs (16.5% conv), rev $4,769 (251 payments)
- New config (effective day36+): ads $2,280/day (content_mktg S1 1300, referral S1 900,
  linkedin D_E09/D_E02 40 each), dev $2,420/day (global 2000 + targeted 420), ops $700/day,
  capacity Tier1 $215/day
- cpl this week: content_marketing $5.96/lead, referral_program $6.36/lead (IMPROVING
  with scale, likely due to reputation boost from social posts)
- Monthly churn signal: 1/14 from day1-7 cohort's first billing (very small sample!)
- R&D tier1 (+0.0289 quality) completes day37 (mid next week)
"""
import random

random.seed(42)

def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl, ad_growth_rate,
             ad_plateau_week, n_weeks=26, starting_cash=500547.0, starting_subs=423,
             price=19.0, verbose=False):
    cash = starting_cash
    subs = starting_subs
    ad_spend = 2200.0  # content+referral combined for S1, starting point
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30)
    cash_trace = []
    # track cohort ages for rebilling approximation: list of (subs_count, week_joined)
    cohorts = [(starting_subs, 0)]

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # ad spend growth strategy: grow until plateau week, then hold flat (roughly)
        if w <= ad_plateau_week:

Week 5 (day35) forecast model v2 -- WITH ADAPTIVE SPEND CONTROL.
v1 (forecast_model_wk5.py) showed that blind exponential ad-spend growth bankrupts
the company even in "bull" scenarios, because CAC is paid upfront but LTV is
collected as $19/mo over many months -- classic SaaS cash-flow trap. A real CEO
(me) would throttle spend based on runway. This version encodes that discipline:
each week, only grow ad spend if projected runway stays above a floor; otherwise
hold flat or cut back. This matches my actual stated strategy in MEMORY.md.
"""

def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl,
             runway_floor_weeks, max_weekly_ad_growth,
             n_weeks=26, starting_cash=500547.0, starting_subs=423,
             price=19.0, verbose=False):
    cash = starting_cash
    subs = starting_subs
    ad_spend = 2200.0
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30)
    cash_trace = []
    cohorts = [(starting_subs, 0)]
    fixed_other = 2420 + 700  # dev + ops (capacity handled separately)

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # --- estimate current weekly burn at present ad_spend to decide on growth ---
        usage_per_day_now = subs * 82
        if usage_per_day_now < 45000:
            cap_cost_now = 215
        elif usage_per_day_now < 180000:
            cap_cost_now = 530
        elif usage_per_day_now < 560000:
            cap_cost_now = 1330
        else:
            cap_cost_now = 4000
        est_weekly_cost = (ad_spend + fixed_other + cap_cost_now) * 7 + usage_per_day_now * 0.002 * 7
        est_weekly_rev = subs * (price / 4.3)  # rough steady-state revenue approx
        est_weekly_burn = max(est_weekly_cost - est_weekly_rev, 1000)
        runway_weeks = cash / est_weekly_burn

        # adaptive growth: full growth rate if runway is healthy, taper/cut if not
        if runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks * 1.5:
            growth = max_weekly_ad_growth
        elif runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks:
            growth = max_weekly_ad_growth * 0.4
        elif runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks * 0.6:
            growth = 0.0  # hold flat
        else:
            growth = -0.30  # cut back hard

        ad_spend = max(ad_spend * (1 + growth), 500.0)

        scale_factor = ad_spend / 2200.0
        cpl = cpl_base * (1 + cpl_degradation_per_dbl * max(0, (scale_factor - 1)))
        leads = ad_spend / cpl
        organic_leads = subs * 0.002 * 7
        total_leads = leads + organic_leads
        new_subs = total_leads * conv_rate

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append((new_subs, w))

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for (csize, joined_week) in cohorts:
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * price

        revenue = new_subs * price + rebill_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_cost = 2420 * 7
        ops_cost = 700 * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * 82
        if usage_per_day < 45000:
            cap_cost = 215
        elif usage_per_day < 180000:
            cap_cost = 530
        elif usage_per_day < 560000:
            cap_cost = 1330
        else:
            cap_cost = 4000
        capacity_cost = cap_cost * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * 0.002 * 7
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * 0.5

        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_cost + ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        # R&D: only invest a tier if cash comfortably above a high bar, capped once per run
        rd_cost = 0.0
        if w in (4, 12) and cash > 900000:
            rd_cost = 333333

        research_cost = 25000 * 0.7  # ~0.7 attempts/week average

        cash = cash + revenue - total_cost - rd_cost - research_cost
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w}: subs={subs:.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:.0f} runway={runway_weeks:.1f} "
                  f"leads={total_leads:.0f} new_subs={new_subs:.0f} rev={revenue:.0f} "
                  f"cost={total_cost:.0f} rd={rd_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")

    return cash_trace

             n_weeks=26, starting_cash=500547.0 - 1820*0, starting_subs=423,

    def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
        if usage_per_day < 45000:

"""
Week 5 (day35) forecast model v4 -- fixed so week1 uses the ACTUAL committed ad_spend
(2280/day) rather than an already-grown value. Growth decisions (representing my own
future weekly adaptive choices) apply starting week 2 onward.
"""

def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl,
             runway_floor_weeks, max_weekly_ad_growth,
             n_weeks=26, starting_cash=500547.22, starting_subs=423,
             price=19.0, verbose=False, rd_investment_week=None, rd_cost=333333,
             rd_cash_bar=850000):
    cash = starting_cash
    subs = starting_subs
    ad_spend = 2280.0  # actual committed level for days 36-42
    dev_ops_fixed = 600 + 700
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30)
    cash_trace = []
    cohorts = [(starting_subs, 0)]

    def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
        if usage_per_day < 45000:
            return 215
        elif usage_per_day < 180000:
            return 530
        elif usage_per_day < 560000:
            return 1330
        else:
            return 4000

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        if w > 1:
            # decide growth for weeks 2+ based on runway at start of this week
            usage_per_day_now = subs * 82
            cap_cost_now = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day_now)
            est_weekly_cost = (ad_spend + dev_ops_fixed + cap_cost_now) * 7 + usage_per_day_now * 0.002 * 7
            est_weekly_rev = subs * (price / 4.3)
            est_weekly_burn = max(est_weekly_cost - est_weekly_rev, 1000)
            runway_weeks = cash / est_weekly_burn

            if runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks * 1.5:
                growth = max_weekly_ad_growth
            elif runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks:
                growth = max_weekly_ad_growth * 0.4
            elif runway_weeks > runway_floor_weeks * 0.6:
                growth = 0.0
            else:
                growth = -0.30
            ad_spend = max(ad_spend * (1 + growth), 500.0)
        else:
            runway_weeks = cash / 25000  # rough placeholder, unused for w==1 decision

        scale_factor = ad_spend / 2280.0
        cpl = cpl_base * (1 + cpl_degradation_per_dbl * max(0, (scale_factor - 1)))
        leads = ad_spend / cpl
        organic_leads = subs * 0.002 * 7
        total_leads = leads + organic_leads
        new_subs = total_leads * conv_rate

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append((new_subs, w))

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for (csize, joined_week) in cohorts:
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * price

        revenue = new_subs * price + rebill_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * 82
        cap_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day)
        capacity_cost = cap_cost * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * 0.002 * 7
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * 0.5

        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        rd_spend = 0.0
        if rd_investment_week is not None and w == rd_investment_week and cash > rd_cash_bar:
            rd_spend = rd_cost

        research_cost = 25000 * 0.6

        cash = cash + revenue - total_cost - rd_spend - research_cost
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w}: subs={subs:.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:.0f} "
                  f"leads={total_leads:.0f} new_subs={new_subs:.0f} rev={revenue:.0f} "
                  f"cost={total_cost:.0f} rd={rd_spend:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(monthly_churn=0.25, conv_rate=0.11, cpl_base=7.0, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.20,
                 runway_floor_weeks=14, max_weekly_ad_growth=0.15, rd_investment_week=None),
    "base": dict(monthly_churn=0.10, conv_rate=0.15, cpl_base=6.2, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.12,
                 runway_floor_weeks=12, max_weekly_ad_growth=0.20, rd_investment_week=8),
    "bull": dict(monthly_churn=0.05, conv_rate=0.18, cpl_base=5.8, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.05,
                 runway_floor_weeks=10, max_weekly_ad_growth=0.25, rd_investment_week=6),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory

## Game basics (confirmed from live API)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. Currently **day35, cash $500,547** (post wk5 actions incl $25K research spend).
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk).
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE at any moment.**
- **`predictions` table stores ALL past forecasts** — query it directly (`SELECT submit_day, horizon_days, predicted_value, predicted_lower, predicted_upper FROM predictions`) instead of relying on memory to check calibration! Much more reliable.
- CONFIG LAG: actions taken on "Day N" session apply to days N+1...N+7. No lag loss if acting once/week right after dashboard.
- market_research(): $25K/attempt, ~30% chance, discovers random undiscovered group. Cumulative as of day35: **9 attempts, 4 successes** (D_E09 wk0, D_E02 wk2, D_S07 wk4, D_S10 wk5). Still keep doing ~1/wk — cheap optionality, each success is a free new data point even if most fail to convert.
- R&D: 20 tiers. Tier1 ($166,667, sampled +0.0289 boost) in progress since day7, **completes day37 (early THIS coming week)** — first real ROI data point, check next session!
- Query `SELECT * FROM research_projects` for ACTUAL sampled values per invocation (not tier-level means).

## ⭐⭐ BIG STRATEGIC INSIGHT (day35): cash-flow trap of low-ARPU growth + fixed dev/ops cost
Built a real week-by-week simulation model (forecast_model_wk5d.py, bug-fixed version) varying churn/conversion/ad-efficiency across bear/base/bull scenarios. Key findings:
1. **Blindly growing ad spend exponentially bankrupts the company even in "bull" cases** — CAC is paid upfront (~$36-40/subscriber) but LTV is collected as $19/mo over many months. Cash-flow timing matters more than LTV/CAC ratio alone.
2. **Fixed dev+ops costs must scale with revenue base, not be a flat large number.** At $2470/day dev + $550/day ops (wk4 levels), breakeven required ~5,267 subscribers just to cover fixed costs via steady-state rebill revenue (subs×$19/mo). We only had 423. **Cut global dev 2000→500/day and killed low-value targeted dev (D_S07, D_E09/D_E02 group-bonus bets) → new breakeven ≈3,200-3,800 subs**, much more reachable. Freed ~$1,820/day.
3. Rationale for WHY dev spend wasn't earning its keep: S1 (our only real revenue source) already clears its q_min (0.081) by a HUGE margin (delivered 0.1966, gap unchanged from day28→day35 — **no expectation drift detected yet**), so more global dev barely helps S1 convert/retain. Meanwhile S2/D_S07/D_S10 need +0.05-0.10 MORE quality just to clear their zero-price bar — log-saturation math shows $300/day targeted dev takes MONTHS to close that gap. **R&D lump-sum investments are the efficient path to unlock quality-gated segments, not incremental dev spend.**
4. **Model shows cash trending toward zero/negative by week ~12-26 under a naive "throttle ad spend when runway gets low" policy**, even after the dev cut — because capacity tier is a STEP function (cost jumps discretely as usage crosses tier boundaries) creating lumpy margins, and S1's ARPU ($19/mo) is just low relative to fixed infra costs at the tier needed for thousands of subscribers.
5. **Action implication going forward:** (a) keep dev/ops LEAN, scale them with revenue not blindly, (b) watch for the moment S1 growth decelerates or margins compress and be ready to cut ad spend harder/faster than "gently", (c) seriously consider a real R&D bet (tier 3-6) in the next few weeks IF tier1's result (landing day37) looks good, since unlocking S2 (WTP $178.59, 5.2x more revenue/sub than S1!) or S3 (WTP $192.98) would be transformative for the whole unit-economics picture, (d) keep pushing market_research to find more S1-like winners among 16 remaining undiscovered groups — need volume of winners, not just one.

## Segment status (day35 delivered quality: base=0.20, global_bonus=0.0621 — will grow slower now at $500/day dev)
| Group | q_min ($0,±65%) | Max delivered (plan/tier) | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 (cap 272,812, WTP $25.87) | **0.081 — unchanged since day28, NO drift yet** | 0.2621(B,T4), using A@0.1966 | **PROVEN WINNER.** Conversion IMPROVED to 16.5% (was 12%) at 2280/day combined ad spend (up 63% from 1400) — efficiency IMPROVED not degraded (content_mktg $5.96/lead vs $6.38 prior; referral $6.36/lead vs $7.16 prior). Likely reputation-boost effect from social posts. | **Keep scaling, watch for first sign of degradation** |
| D_S07 (cap 52,655, WTP $94.54) | 0.195 | 0.2636(B,T4)/0.1977(A,T2) | **KILLED day35: 0/32 conversions after full week pilot ($700 spent).** Binomial: P(0/32) if true rate=10% is only 3.4% → strong evidence this segment doesn't really clear its price-scaled bar. Same failure pattern as S3. | $0 ads/dev now. Group bonus (+0.0016, tiny) persists harmlessly |
| **D_S10 (NEW day35, cap 55,074, WTP $99.49)** | 0.297 (HIGHER bar than D_S07 had, and D_S07 already failed at a lower bar) | ~0.2621 (B,T4) max currently — i.e. **below q_min point estimate already** | New discovery, "Music Producers". Has organic network inflow from S1 (rate 0.0029/sub/day → ~1.2 leads/day for FREE at 423 S1 subs, growing with S1 base) | **$0 ad/dev spend — let organic network leads test this for FREE** (learned from D_S07: don't pay to pilot an unproven segment when organic data is free). Only invest if organic leads show ANY conversions. |
| S2 (cap 167,374, WTP $178.59) | 0.37 | 0.3034(B,T4) | Below q_min. Highest-ARPU realistic target (5.2x S1's revenue/sub) | $0 ads, $100/day dev (trimmed from 300, minimal optionality only — real unlock needs R&D not dev grind) |
| S3 (cap 65,292, WTP $192.98) | 0.145 | 0.3212(B,T4) | Proven unconvertible (0/64 wk3) despite clearing q_min@$0 — price-scaled bar too steep | $0 ads/dev |
| D_E09 (ent, cap 53) | 0.199 | 0.2736(B,T4) | 0 leads via paid ($2,800 spent, 5 wks). **1 ORGANIC lead via 'network' channel day32** (customer 2976) — no subscription/enterprise_turn created yet, still watching | $40/day linkedin lottery ticket. Cut targeted dev (was 60/day, not the bottleneck — lead FLOW is) |
| D_E02 (ent, cap 179) | 0.219 | 0.2689(B,T4) | 0 leads ever, any channel, any time | $40/day linkedin lottery ticket only |
| E1/E2/E3 | 0.736/1.094/0.668 | ~0.2621 | Impossible even at noise floor | $0 ads/dev |
| enterprise_turns table | — | — | **STILL 0 ROWS EVER (day35)** — even the 1 organic D_E09 lead hasn't generated a turn | Keep checking weekly |

## Churn data (CRITICAL — still tiny sample, don't over-index)
- Day1-7 cohort (created_day≤7): 170 total leads → only 14 EVER subscribed (156 lost on arrival, expected — q_min bar). Of those 14: **1 cancelled after first 30-day billing (~7.1% monthly churn), 13 still active** as of day35.
- This is a GOOD sign (low churn) but n=14 is way too small to trust. Keep tracking as more cohorts hit their 30/60/90-day billing marks over the next several weeks — this determines whether LTV/CAC (~7x at 7% churn, ~1.6x even at 30% churn) really holds.

## Quality dynamics — formula (confirmed, from docs/api/marketing.json)
- Global: `0.006 × ln(1 + global_daily_spend/5000)`/day, all groups, permanent. At NEW $500/day: only 0.006×ln(1.1)=0.00057/day (~0.004/wk) — much slower than the $2000/day rate (~0.0115-0.0147/wk actually observed). Accept slower quality growth for S1 (huge buffer) in exchange for cash runway.
- Targeted per-group: `0.030 × ln(1 + targeted_spend/5000)`/day, stacks additively, PERSISTS after spend stops.
- delivered_quality = (base 0.20 + global_bonus + group_bonus) × tier_multiplier. Tier mult: T1=.6,T2=.75,T3=.9,T4=1.0,T5=1.1.

## Cost reference (get_cost_info)
- Model tier cost_per_usage_unit: T1=$0.0003,T2=$0.002,T3=$0.006,T4=$0.012,T5=$0.03/unit. S1 is virtually 100% Plan A (T2, $0.002/unit, $19/mo) — confirmed via query.
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K/$85/day, T1=200K/$215/day, T2=800K/$530/day, T3=2.5M/$1330/day, T4=8M/$4000/day.
- **Upgraded T0→T1 day35**: usage hit 31,595/day (63% of T0 cap) with growth accelerating (subs nearly tripled in a week) — proactive upgrade before overload, only +$130/day. Also 4 social posts day35 complained about slowness/quality dip, correlating with capacity strain (though DB shows delivered quality still RISING — likely flavor text tied to expectation drift, not literal quality drop; capacity was the real risk).
- Issue resolution: flat ~1-day resolution confirmed in DB historically. Ops raised 550→700/day this week (open issues grew to 46, want to stay ahead as scale continues + outage-probability insurance now that we're pushing usage harder).
- Ops/outage formula (confirmed docs): outage prob ~3%/day at $0 ops, ~1.1%/day at $500. Issue resolution: Poisson((base_rate+scale_g×spend)×n_g/total_open), scale_g=0.3 individual/0.05 enterprise per $ — i.e. ops $ helps individual-group issues 6x more efficiently than enterprise per dollar (moot for us now since ~0 enterprise subs).

## Ad channel efficiency (S1), empirical $/lead by week
| Week (spend/day: content/referral) | content_marketing | referral_program |
|---|---|---|
| $50/$40 (wk1) | $6.73 | $6.22 |
| $100/$80 (wk2) | $7.14 | $6.83 |
| $280/$180 (wk3) | $7.10 | $6.96 |
| $450/$320 (wk4) | $6.38 | $7.16 |
| $720/$500 (wk5) | **$5.96** | **$6.36** |
- Efficiency IMPROVED at higher scale in wk5 (opposite of normal diminishing returns) — hypothesis: reputation boost from social media replies (wk4, wk5) improved both lead arrival speed AND conversion rate (16.5% this week vs ~12% prior weeks) simultaneously. **Wk5 action: scaled further to content=$1300, referral=$900 (both +80%).** Will check wk6 dashboard for continued efficiency/conversion trend — first sign of REAL diminishing returns or conversion-rate reversion should trigger throttling.
- search_ads/social_media killed wk4 (2-3x worse $/lead) — still dead, not revisited.

## Actions Log (condensed)
- **Wk0-4:** see git history. Summary: Prices A=$19,B=$99,C=$179 (T2/T4/T3, quotas 200/280/800). S3 promo experiment failed conclusively (0/64). Enterprise ads reduced to $40/day linkedin-only lottery tickets. First 2 social posts (wk3, wk4 replies to complaints) both well-received, boosted reputation/conversion.
- **Wk5 (day35):** Cash $553,349→$525,547 (dashboard, pre-actions) →$500,547 (post $25K research). Individual subs 423 (+242 this wk, 16.5% conv of 1463 leads). Actions taken:
  - **Capacity: Tier0→Tier1** ($85→$215/day) — usage was 63% of T0 cap, growing fast.
  - **Killed D_S07 pilot** (0/32 conversions, statistically strong failure signal) — freed $150/day.
  - **Scaled S1 ads further**: content_marketing $720→$1300, referral_program $500→$900 (both +~80%). Total ads now $2,280/day (was $1,400).
  - **MAJOR: cut dev spend 2470→600/day** (global 2000→500, targeted: killed D_S07/D_E09/D_E02 group-bonus bets, kept only S2 optionality trimmed 300→100) after modeling revealed dev spend wasn't earning its keep relative to revenue base (see Big Strategic Insight above). Freed $1,870/day.
  - **Ops 550→700/day** (issue count growing to 46, more insurance as we scale usage harder).
  - market_research → SUCCESS, discovered **D_S10 "Music Producers"** (cap 55,074, WTP $99.49, q_min 0.297 — HIGHER bar than D_S07 which already failed at a lower bar). Decided: $0 spend, monitor free organic network leads only (S1→D_S10 referral rate 0.0029/sub/day).
  - Social post #3: replied to a "quality dip / slowness" complaint (post 46) referencing the REAL capacity upgrade + R&D tier1 landing this week — both true, backed-up claims (learned from past: authentic/backed claims land better than generic reassurance).
  - New daily fixed cost: ads 2280+dev 600+ops 700+capacity 215 = **$3,795/day** (LOWER than wk4's $4,505/day despite the ad increase, thanks to the dev cut).

## To-Do / Check every week
1. **R&D tier1 completes ~day37 (this coming week!) — check `SELECT * FROM research_projects` for quality_boost_applied.** First real R&D ROI data. If it looks good, seriously consider a bigger tier (3-6) investment in the next couple weeks — modeling shows unlocking S2 (5.2x ARPU vs S1) could be transformative, more efficient than dev-spend grinding.
2. Track churn: query day8-14, day15-21 cohorts' first-30-day-billing outcomes as they come due (day38-44, day45-51 respectively) — need much bigger n than the current 14.

"""
Week 6 (day42) forecast model.
Confirmed mechanic this week: billing is IMMEDIATE on signup (day=start_day) + every 30 days after.
So weekly revenue = new_subs_this_week * price + recurring_rebills_from_cohorts_hitting_30day_marks.

Calibration data (day42 actuals):
- subs: 966 (up from 423 last week)
- leads this week: 2306, new subs: 545 (conv rate 23.7% blended, content=23.7%, referral=23.0%)
- ad spend was 2200/day (content 1300 + referral 900) -> leads 2233 (content 1423 + referral 810), rest organic/other groups
- $/lead: content 6.40, referral 7.78 (degrading at margin, referral worse)
- usage: 337,420 units/wk = 48,203/day over avg ~694 subs during the week => ~69.4 units/day/sub
- compute cost: $0.002/unit (T2, all Plan A)
- revenue this week: $10,678 = 545*19 (10355, immediate) + ~17 recurring old-cohort rebills (323)
- capacity Tier1 (200K cap, $215/day), current utilization 24%
- ops $700/day keeps issue resolution flat at 1.0 day avg even as issues doubled -> not a binding constraint
- dev cut to 500->200/day global (post this week's action), S2/enterprise targeted spend killed
"""
import random

random.seed(42)

PRICE = 19.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002
USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY = 69.4
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]

def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.95:  # upgrade proactively before hitting 95% to avoid overload
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]


def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl,
             ad_growth_rate, ad_growth_cap_week, organic_rate, dev_ops_fixed,
             research_market_weeks, rd_plan, n_weeks=26, start_ad_spend=3050.0,
             start_subs=966.0, start_cash=482831.0 - 25000.0,  # this session's research_market cost
             verbose=False):
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30.0)
    subs = start_subs
    cash = start_cash
    ad_spend = start_ad_spend
    cohorts = []  # (size, week_joined)
    cash_trace = []

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # ad spend growth policy: grow while cash healthy, throttle if runway gets short
        runway_weeks = cash / max(1.0, (cash_trace[-1] - cash_trace[-2])) if len(cash_trace) >= 2 and cash_trace[-2] > cash_trace[-1] else 999
        if w <= ad_growth_cap_week:
            if cash > 150000:
                ad_spend = ad_spend * (1 + ad_growth_rate)
            elif cash > 50000:
                ad_spend = ad_spend * (1 + ad_growth_rate * 0.3)
            else:
                ad_spend = ad_spend * 0.7  # throttle hard if cash critical

        scale_factor = ad_spend / 3050.0
        cpl = cpl_base * (1 + cpl_degradation_per_dbl * max(0, (scale_factor - 1)))
        leads_paid = (ad_spend / cpl) * 7
        organic_leads = subs * organic_rate * 7
        total_leads = leads_paid + organic_leads
        new_subs = total_leads * conv_rate

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append([new_subs, w])

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for c in cohorts:
            csize, joined_week = c
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:  # ~30 days
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * PRICE

        revenue = new_subs * PRICE + rebill_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day) * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT * 7
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * LEAD_ACQ_COST

        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        research_cost = 25000.0 if w <= research_market_weeks else 0.0

        rd_cost = 0.0
        if rd_plan is not None:
            wk_trigger, cost = rd_plan
            if w == wk_trigger and cash > cost * 1.5:
                rd_cost = cost

        cash = cash + revenue - total_cost - research_cost - rd_cost
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w}: subs={subs:,.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:,.0f} leads={total_leads:,.0f} "
                  f"new_subs={new_subs:,.0f} rev={revenue:,.0f} cost={total_cost:,.0f} cash={cash:,.0f}")

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(monthly_churn=0.20, conv_rate=0.15, cpl_base=7.5, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.25,
                 ad_growth_rate=0.10, ad_growth_cap_week=10, organic_rate=0.0012,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=6, rd_plan=None),
    "base": dict(monthly_churn=0.10, conv_rate=0.21, cpl_base=6.9, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.15,
                 ad_growth_rate=0.20, ad_growth_cap_week=14, organic_rate=0.0018,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=10, rd_plan=(9, 333333)),
    "bull": dict(monthly_churn=0.05, conv_rate=0.25, cpl_base=6.2, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.08,
                 ad_growth_rate=0.28, ad_growth_cap_week=18, organic_rate=0.0025,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=12, rd_plan=(7, 333333)),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE (cash at horizon) ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")

"""
Week 6 (day42) forecast model v2 - reflects an ADAPTIVE manager (me) who monitors
cash weekly and throttles ad spend to maintain a minimum runway buffer, rather than
blindly compounding growth. This is more realistic than wk6.py's crude policy.

Policy: each week, look at trailing net burn rate (excl. ad spend growth itself) to
estimate runway. If runway > target_runway_weeks -> grow ad spend by growth_rate.
If runway between 0.5x-1x target -> hold flat.
If runway < 0.5x target -> cut ad spend by 25%.
Never let ad spend exceed a "sensible" ceiling relative to current sub base (avoid
absurd CAC spirals) - cap growth of new-subs-per-week to at most ~35% of current base.
"""

PRICE = 19.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002
USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY = 69.4
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
TARGET_RUNWAY_WEEKS = 10.0

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]

def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]


def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl,
             growth_rate, organic_rate, dev_ops_fixed,
             research_market_weeks, rd_plan,
             n_weeks=26, start_ad_spend=3050.0, start_subs=966.0,
             start_cash=482831.0 - 25000.0, verbose=False):
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30.0)
    subs = start_subs
    cash = start_cash
    ad_spend = start_ad_spend
    cohorts = []
    cash_trace = []
    net_burn_hist = []

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # --- adaptive ad spend policy based on trailing runway ---
        if net_burn_hist:
            trailing_burn = sum(net_burn_hist[-3:]) / len(net_burn_hist[-3:])
        else:
            trailing_burn = 20000.0  # prior guess before any data
        runway = cash / trailing_burn if trailing_burn > 100 else 999
        if runway > TARGET_RUNWAY_WEEKS:
            ad_spend *= (1 + growth_rate)
        elif runway > TARGET_RUNWAY_WEEKS * 0.5:
            pass  # hold flat
        else:
            ad_spend *= 0.75  # cut hard to preserve cash
        ad_spend = max(ad_spend, 500.0)

        scale_factor = ad_spend / 3050.0
        cpl = cpl_base * (1 + cpl_degradation_per_dbl * max(0, (scale_factor - 1)))
        leads_paid = (ad_spend / cpl) * 7
        organic_leads = subs * organic_rate * 7
        total_leads = leads_paid + organic_leads
        new_subs = total_leads * conv_rate
        # sanity cap: can't plausibly grow more than 40%/week from a cold-start market
        new_subs = min(new_subs, subs * 0.40 + 50)

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append([new_subs, w])

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for c in cohorts:
            csize, joined_week = c
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * PRICE

        revenue = new_subs * PRICE + rebill_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day) * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT * 7
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * LEAD_ACQ_COST
        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        research_cost = 25000.0 if w <= research_market_weeks else 0.0
        rd_cost = 0.0
        if rd_plan is not None:
            wk_trigger, cost = rd_plan
            if w == wk_trigger and cash > cost * 1.8:
                rd_cost = cost

        net = revenue - total_cost - research_cost - rd_cost
        cash = cash + net
        net_burn_hist.append(-net)  # positive = burn
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w:2d}: subs={subs:8,.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:7,.0f} leads={total_leads:7,.0f} "
                  f"new_subs={new_subs:6,.0f} rev={revenue:9,.0f} cost={total_cost:9,.0f} "
                  f"net={net:9,.0f} cash={cash:11,.0f} runway_wk={runway:5.1f}")

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(monthly_churn=0.20, conv_rate=0.14, cpl_base=7.6, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.22,
                 growth_rate=0.08, organic_rate=0.0010,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=4, rd_plan=None),
    "base": dict(monthly_churn=0.10, conv_rate=0.20, cpl_base=6.9, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.14,
                 growth_rate=0.14, organic_rate=0.0017,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=8, rd_plan=(10, 333333)),
    "bull": dict(monthly_churn=0.06, conv_rate=0.25, cpl_base=6.3, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.08,
                 growth_rate=0.18, organic_rate=0.0024,
                 dev_ops_fixed=900, research_market_weeks=12, rd_plan=(8, 333333)),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE (cash at horizon) ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")

"""
Week 6 (day42) forecast model v3.
Calibrated against ACTUAL observed weekly subscribed-count trajectory:
  day7=12, day14=29, day21=79, day28=179, day35=421, day42=966
  (ratios: 2.42x, 2.72x, 2.27x, 2.35x, 2.29x per week - driven by MY OWN aggressive
   ad-spend increases 50-80%/week during that period, NOT organic alone)

This week I'm increasing ad spend more modestly (+38.6%: 2200->3050/day) after killing
dead spend (enterprise ads, S2 dev). Going forward I plan to keep scaling but at a
DECAYING growth rate (moderating from here) both because (a) I will choose to grow
spend less aggressively per-week than the last 4 weeks, and (b) per-channel CPL
degradation + eventual market-cap saturation (S1 cap ~273K, currently 966 = 0.35%,
so cap isn't binding yet at this horizon but will matter by month 4-6 if growth stays
explosive).

Key confirmed mechanics:
- Billing: IMMEDIATE $19 on signup + every 30 days after (NOT lagged).
- $/lead this week: content_marketing $6.40, referral_program $7.78 (blended $6.90).
  Conversion rate 23.7% blended (up from 16.5% last week) - reputation/quality tailwind.
- Usage ~69.4 units/day/sub, compute $0.002/unit (T2).
- Fixed costs after this week's cuts: ops $700/day + dev $200/day = $900/day.
"""

PRICE = 19.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
S1_MARKET_CAP = 272812.0

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]

def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]


def simulate(monthly_churn, conv_rate, cpl_base, cpl_degradation_per_dbl,
             initial_ad_growth, ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth,
             organic_rate_per_sub, usage_per_sub, dev_ops_fixed,
             research_weeks, rd_plan, n_weeks=26,
             start_ad_spend=3050.0, start_subs=966.0,
             start_cash=482831.0 - 25000.0, verbose=False):
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30.0)
    subs = start_subs
    cash = start_cash
    ad_spend = start_ad_spend
    ad_growth = initial_ad_growth
    cohorts = []
    cash_trace = []

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # ad spend grows each week but growth rate decays toward a floor (my own throttling)
        # also throttle harder if cash is getting thin
        if cash < 100000:
            ad_growth_eff = -0.20
        elif cash < 200000:
            ad_growth_eff = min(ad_growth, 0.03)
        else:
            ad_growth_eff = ad_growth
        ad_spend = max(ad_spend * (1 + ad_growth_eff), 400.0)
        ad_growth = max(ad_growth * ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth)

        scale_factor = ad_spend / 3050.0
        cpl = cpl_base * (1 + cpl_degradation_per_dbl * max(0, (scale_factor - 1)))
        leads_paid = (ad_spend / cpl) * 7
        organic_leads = subs * organic_rate_per_sub * 7
        raw_new_subs = (leads_paid + organic_leads) * conv_rate

        # market saturation dampening (soft), negligible until subs is a meaningful % of cap
        headroom = max(0.0, 1 - (subs / S1_MARKET_CAP) ** 1.5)
        new_subs = raw_new_subs * headroom

        total_leads = leads_paid + organic_leads
        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append([new_subs, w])

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for c in cohorts:
            csize, joined_week = c
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * PRICE

        revenue = new_subs * PRICE + rebill_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * usage_per_sub
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day) * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT * 7
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * LEAD_ACQ_COST
        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        research_cost = 25000.0 if w <= research_weeks else 0.0
        rd_cost = 0.0
        if rd_plan is not None:
            wk_trigger, cost = rd_plan
            if w == wk_trigger and cash > cost * 1.8:
                rd_cost = cost

        net = revenue - total_cost - research_cost - rd_cost
        cash = cash + net
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w:2d}: subs={subs:9,.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:7,.0f} leads={total_leads:7,.0f} "
                  f"new_subs={new_subs:6,.0f} rev={revenue:9,.0f} cost={total_cost:9,.0f} "
                  f"net={net:9,.0f} cash={cash:11,.0f}")

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(monthly_churn=0.20, conv_rate=0.15, cpl_base=7.5, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.20,
                 initial_ad_growth=0.15, ad_growth_decay=0.75, min_ad_growth=0.01,
                 organic_rate_per_sub=0.0012, usage_per_sub=75, dev_ops_fixed=900,
                 research_weeks=3, rd_plan=None),
    "base": dict(monthly_churn=0.09, conv_rate=0.21, cpl_base=6.9, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.13,
                 initial_ad_growth=0.25, ad_growth_decay=0.82, min_ad_growth=0.02,
                 organic_rate_per_sub=0.0020, usage_per_sub=70, dev_ops_fixed=900,
                 research_weeks=6, rd_plan=(12, 333333)),
    "bull": dict(monthly_churn=0.05, conv_rate=0.26, cpl_base=6.3, cpl_degradation_per_dbl=0.07,
                 initial_ad_growth=0.35, ad_growth_decay=0.88, min_ad_growth=0.04,
                 organic_rate_per_sub=0.0030, usage_per_sub=65, dev_ops_fixed=900,
                 research_weeks=8, rd_plan=(8, 333333)),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE (cash at horizon) ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory

## Game basics (confirmed from live API)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day49, cash $393,228.74** (post wk7 actions — see mistake below).
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE at any moment.**
- Billing is IMMEDIATE on signup ($19 Plan A day 1) + recurring every 30 days after (`billing_day_mod30`). Confirmed multiple weeks running.
- Ledger entries for INSTANT actions (market_research, research_group, research_project) post at the CURRENT day, immediately reducing cash BEFORE the next week's simulation runs.
- `service_day` table has exact daily usage/capacity/latency/error data — use this (not just the weekly aggregate) to see WITHIN-week trend and spot accelerating usage early.
- `ads_revenue` table confirms ads_strength formula precisely: **effective = log10(1 + 9×strength)**. Verified: strength=0.10 → avg_strength recorded 0.2788 = log10(1.9). NOTE: the API doc's own example ("0.1→0.40 effective") appears to be a TYPO/wrong — 0.5→0.74 and 1.0→1.0 DO match the log10(1+9x) formula exactly, but 0.1 should give 0.279, not 0.40. Trust the formula + the 0.5/1.0 anchors, not the 0.1 example.
- R&D: 20 tiers total (confirmed via `list_research_projects`). Costs: T1=$166,667(done,+0.0289 actual), T2=$333,333(mean+0.07,~17d), T3=$500,000(mean+0.11,~23d), T4=$666,667(mean+0.16), T5=$833,333(mean+0.22)... up to T20. Cost-per-quality-point improves at higher tiers but absolute cost/duration also rises a lot.
- research_market(): $25K/attempt, ~30% stated chance. Cumulative as of day49: **11 attempts, 5 successes (45%)**. 15 groups remain undiscovered (of 26 total: 6 initial + 20 discoverable).
- research_group(): Level2=$60K, Level3=$175K, Level4=$350K, Level5=$700K. Works on ANY group incl. initial S1-S3/E1-E3 (confirmed: `get_market_overview` shows info_level=1/±65% noise for ALL groups, including the "initial 6" — they are NOT fully known/exact as the generic game overview doc implies. Always verify via live `get_group_insights`, don't trust generic instructions blindly).

## ⚠️⚠️ MISTAKE THIS WEEK (day49) — DO NOT REPEAT
**Called `research_market()` TWICE in the same session — once in the main action script, then AGAIN just to "see the result/confirm success" in a follow-up verification script. This is a PAID ACTION ($25K) — calling it again re-triggers the charge, it does NOT just re-report the prior result!** Wasted $25,000 for nothing (both attempts failed anyway — bad luck compounding the error). **RULE: after ANY paid instant action (research_market, research_group, start_research_project), NEVER call the function again to "check" what happened — always verify via `nm.query()` against the relevant table instead** (`segment_discovery` for market research, `research_projects` for R&D). Read-only queries are always free.

## ⭐ BIG PICTURE STATUS (day49): hyper-growth continues, but cracks appearing in the "S1-only" thesis
- Individual subs: 966(day42) → **1842(day49)**, +90.7%/week (still huge, though decelerating from prior weeks' 128%/~2.3x). New leads 3312, new subs 877, blended conversion **26.5%** (up again from 23.7% last week — 5th straight week of improving conversion, driven by compounding quality/reputation gains).
- **NEW: S3 and D_S10 are now converting for real (not just 0-signal anymore):**
  - **S3: 3/10 leads converted this week (30%!), all-time now 3/182.** All 3 conversions happened THIS week only (2 on Plan A, 1 on Plan B $99) — pure organic, $0 ad spend, $0 dev spend until this week. This is a genuine quality-threshold crossing for a slice of S3 (high WTP $193, small cap 65K).
  - **D_S10: 3/11 this week (27%), all-time 4/14 (28.6%).** Consistent conversion rate across multiple weeks now — this is a real, working segment, still 100% organic/network so far.
  - S2 and D_S07 remain proven-unconvertible-so-far: S2 0/44 lifetime (0/2 this wk), D_S07 0/37 lifetime (0/2 this wk).
- **ROOT CAUSE FOUND for why S3/S2 struggled: Plan C was STRICTLY DOMINATED by Plan B** (C: $179, T3→0.9x mult vs B: $99, T4→1.0x mult — C cost MORE for LOWER quality). Result: Plan C had **ZERO subscribers EVER** across the whole game to this point. Fixed this week (see actions).
- Usage/capacity: day49 daily usage spiked to 137,996 units = **69% of Tier1's 200K cap** (up from ~37-45K/day just 2 weeks prior) — upgraded to Tier2 this week before overload hit (see actions).
- Enterprise still totally dead: enterprise_turns table = 0 rows ever after 7 weeks. Zero enterprise leads again this week. Continue ignoring.
- Ops/issues: 175 open issues (up from 91), but resolution time still ~same-day flat (avg days_open ~0.0007-0.0012 across 1,526 resolved + 835 resolved this week alone) — $700/day ops still has huge headroom.
- Social media sentiment: net positive this week — organic post bragging that a competitor's support "ghosted for days" while NovaMind "responded within hours". Some mild latency complaints ("interface got clunkier... response times slowing") consistent with the capacity crunch — upgrading Tier2 should help. No formal "competitor event" notification seen yet (macro still PMI 48.9 "declining", unchanged since day31).

## Week 7 (day49) actions taken
1. **Capacity Tier1→Tier2** (800K cap, $530/day, was $215/day, +$315/day): usage hit 69% of Tier1 cap on day49 alone and accelerating — proactive upgrade before overload/outage.
2. **Fixed Plan C tier: T3→T5** (1.1x mult, was 0.9x — C was strictly dominated by B despite costing more, 0 subs ever). New Plan C delivered quality for e.g. S3 = (0.20+0.101+0.0592)×1.1≈0.396, S2 = (0.20+0.101+0.0445)×1.1≈0.380 — **S2's noisy q_min estimate is 0.37, so this might JUST tip S2 into convertible range for the first time.** This is the single highest-leverage change this week if it works (S2 market cap 167K, much bigger than S3's 65K).
3. **Trimmed Plan C quota 800→500** units/day to bound compute-cost tail risk now that C runs at the expensive T5 rate ($0.03/unit). Observed real per-customer usage (S3 Plan-B customer: 113-188/day) is well under quota ceilings generally, so this is a conservative guardrail, not expected to bind.
4. **Ad spend scaled up + diversified**: S1 content_marketing $2100→$2600, referral_program $950→$1300 (continuing the proven engine — conversion still rising, marginal cost still reasonable). **NEW test budgets**: S3 ($120 content+$60 referral=$180/day), D_S10 ($70+$50=$120/day), S2 ($70+$50=$120/day, betting on the Plan C fix). Total ad spend $3,050→**$4,320/day** (+41.6%).
5. **ads_strength S1: 0.10→0.30** (clean results last week: +$230.54 ad_revenue, only 1 cancellation ALL WEEK out of 1842 subs — no visible harm, scaling up. Effective value goes from 0.279→0.568, ~2x).
6. **Targeted dev spend: added S3 $150/day** (was $0) — cheap 5x-coefficient push now that S3 shows real conversion, to widen the crack further. S1/others unchanged (global dev stays $200/day, S1 still has huge quality buffer).
7. **research_market()** — called (accidentally twice, see mistake above). Both attempts failed this week (0/2). Cumulative 5/11 successes (45%).
8. Ops kept at $700/day, prices/Plan A/B tiers unchanged.

## Segment status snapshot (day49, base=0.20, global_bonus=0.1010 pre-this-week's-dev-effects)
| Group | q_min est (±65%) | Best delivered (plan/tier, OLD config) | Best delivered (NEW: C@T5) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** (cap 272,812, WTP $25.87) | 0.081 | 0.2258 (A,T2) | unchanged | THE business, 1835 active. Conv 26.5% and rising. |
| **S3** (cap 65,292, WTP $192.98) | 0.145 (likely wrong/too low; real bar clearly higher for most) | 0.3602 (B,T4) | **0.396 (C,T5)** | NOW CONVERTING: 3/182 lifetime, 3/10 this wk (30%). Testing paid ads + targeted dev $150/day. |
| **D_S10** (cap 55,074, WTP $99.49) | 0.297 | 0.3010 (A/B similar) | 0.351 (C,T5, if desired — but B likely priced closer to WTP) | Consistently converting 27-33%: 4/14 lifetime. Testing paid ads $120/day. |
| **S2** (cap 167,374, WTP $178.59) | 0.37 (noisy — could be 0.13-0.61) | 0.3455 (B,T4) — below q_min | **0.380 (C,T5) — JUST above q_min estimate!** | 0/44 lifetime but Plan C fix + new $120/day test could change this — WATCH CLOSELY next week. |
| D_S07 (cap 52,655, WTP $94.54) | 0.195 | 0.3026 | 0.335 (C,T5) | Still 0/37 lifetime, $0 spend (no signal yet to justify testing) |
| Enterprise (all) | 0.2-1.1 | ~0.27-0.31 | ~0.31-0.35 | Confirmed dead: 0 leads in 7 weeks, enterprise_turns=0 rows ever |

## R&D strategic thinking
- Tier2 ($333,333) still too large relative to cash ($393K) — would leave dangerously little buffer. Holding off again.
- **BUT: this week's Plan C fix is essentially a FREE quality unlock for S2/S3 (just a tier change, ~$0 marginal cost while Plan C has ~0 subscribers) — a much more capital-efficient way to test the "is S2 close to convertible" hypothesis than spending $60-175K on research_group(S2) or $333K+ on R&D.** If Plan C conversions start appearing for S2 next week or two, that's a strong signal to consider a real R&D tier investment (to push even further) once cash allows. If Plan C does NOT unlock S2 even with real signups, that tells us the gap is bigger than 1 tier level and a bigger R&D bet would be needed to move the needle — decide once we see data.
- Revisit R&D once cash > ~$600-700K OR once we have 1-2 more weeks of Plan-C-conversion data for S2/S3.

## Cost/quality reference (confirmed)
- Model tier cost_per_usage_unit: T1=$0.0003,T2=$0.002,T3=$0.006,T4=$0.012,T5=$0.03/unit. Quality mult: T1=.6,T2=.75,T3=.9,T4=1.0,T5=1.1.
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K/$85/day, T1=200K/$215/day, **T2=800K/$530/day (NOW HERE)**, T3=2.5M/$1330/day, T4=8M/$4000/day, T5=25M/$10K/day, T6=80M/$28K/day, T7=300M/$75K/day.
- Usage/day/sub ≈ 75 units/day (day49: 137,996/1842). At Tier2 (800K), supports ~10,600 subs — should last ~4-5 weeks at current growth rate before needing Tier3. **CHECK `service_day` table WEEKLY, upgrade proactively at ~80% utilization, don't wait for overload flag.**
- Ops $700/day → issue resolution flat at ~same-day even as issue count grows fast — lots of headroom.
- Dev quality formula: global `~0.006 × ln(1+global_spend/5000)`/day (permanent), targeted `~0.030 × ln(1+targeted_spend/5000)`/day per group (persists after spend stops, 5x global coefficient).
- ads_strength: effective = log10(1+9×strength). Generates "ad_revenue" ledger entries; quality/satisfaction cost scales the same way. S1 tested clean at 0.1 (effective 0.279) for a week — no negative signal, scaled to 0.3 (effective 0.568) this week.
- **Plan C was a dominated/dead plan for 7 weeks (T3 mult 0.9 < Plan B's T4 mult 1.0, despite costing more) — always sanity-check that your pricing ladder has monotonically increasing quality with price, or premium plans will never get picked!** Fixed day49 (C→T5). Watch for Plan C uptake next week.

## Ad channel efficiency (S1), $/lead by week
| Week (spend/day: content/referral) | content_marketing | referral_program | blended conv rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| wk5 ($720/$500) | $5.96 | $6.36 | 16.5% |
| wk6 ($1300/$900) | $6.39 avg / $7.02 marginal | $7.78 avg / $10.77 marginal | 23.7% |
| wk7 ($2100/$950) | $6.51 avg / **$6.72 marginal** (IMPROVED vs wk6!) | $7.37 avg (small delta, noisy marginal) | **26.5%** |
| wk8 ($2600/$1300, decided day49) | TBD | TBD | TBD — check next session |
- Conversion rate has now improved 5 weeks straight (12%→12%→12%→16.5%→23.7%→26.5%) while marginal CPL has NOT degraded monotonically (wk7 marginal content CPL improved vs wk6) — reputation/quality compounding is still outrunning ad saturation. **Keep watching for the reversal signal.**
- referral_program conversion (28.2% this wk) now edges out content_marketing (25.8%) for the first time — worth continuing to fund both meaningfully rather than over-indexing on content.

## Forecasting approach
- Model file: `forecast_model_wk7.py` (bear/base/bull scenarios calibrated to day49 actuals). **KNOWN GAP in the model: it doesn't correctly account for the pre-existing 1842-subscriber base's own rolling 30-day rebills in week 1** (only models NEW cohorts formed during the simulation rebilling every 4 weeks) — this understates near-term revenue by roughly the existing-base rebill amount (~$8K/week early on, fading as that cohort's relative weight shrinks). Manually adjusted point estimates upward vs raw model output to compensate, especially for 1wk/4wk.
- The model (like prior weeks') shows a J-curve: cash dips over the next ~2 months of aggressive growth investment before recovering/compounding. Bear case gets uncomfortably low (~$31-70K around week 8-13) — **if actual cash trajectory tracks anywhere near the bear case, THROTTLE AD SPEND HARD well before hitting that level** (don't blindly follow a mechanical ad-spend-growth schedule; watch cash weekly and pull back if it's heading below ~$150-200K with no sign of stabilizing).
- Submitted day49 (for day56/77/133/231): 1wk=$378,000[352K,405K]; 4wk=$230,000[110K,370K]; 12wk=$260,000[40K,620K]; 26wk=$850,000[80K,2,400,000].

## To-Do / Check every week
1. **#1 PRIORITY: check S2 conversion data next week** — did the Plan C (T5) fix + $120/day test ad spend produce ANY S2 signups? This is potentially the biggest lever available (167K market cap, untapped). If yes → consider scaling S2 spend hard and/or a real R&D tier investment. If still 0 → the gap is bigger than 1 tier, hold off further S2 investment pending bigger quality moves.
2. Check S3/D_S10 paid-ad test results — did paid-acquired leads convert at similar rates to the organic ones (30%/28%)? Or lower (as paid leads tend to be less pre-qualified)? Determines whether to scale further.
3. Watch usage vs Tier2 cap (800K) — should have ~4-5 weeks of headroom at current growth, but check `service_day` weekly, don't get complacent.
4. Watch ads_strength=0.3 impact on S1 churn/satisfaction — scale further to 0.4-0.5 if still clean, revert if churn/cancellations tick up.
5. Watch content_marketing vs referral_program marginal cost trend for S1 — 5 weeks running of still-improving conversion; watch for the reversal.
6. Cash discipline: daily recurring costs now ≈ ads $4,320 + ops $700 + dev $350 + capacity $530 = **$5,900/day fixed** + variable (lead_acq ~$300-350/day, compute ~$350-450/day growing). Re-run forecast model each week with fresh actuals.
7. Re-evaluate R&D once cash > ~$600-700K, informed by S2/S3 Plan-C conversion data (see R&D section above).
8. Keep doing research_market() ~1/week — **but query `segment_discovery` table to check results, do NOT call research_market() again just to check the outcome (costs another $25K!).** 15 groups still undiscovered.
9. Check `enterprise_turns` occasionally (0 rows ever after 7 weeks) — deprioritized.
10. Check `get_social_posts` / `macroeconomic_conditions` for competitor events — still just PMI 48.9 "declining", unchanged since day31, no distinct competitor-event notification type seen yet.
11. Query `predictions` table each week for calibration tracking.
12. **Endgame pivot reminder**: around day450-490, stop chasing new-customer growth (CAC won't pay back), shift to pure cash harvesting (cut ad spend, maximize ads_strength/margin). Not relevant yet at day49.

## Mistakes / lessons log
- **NEW (day49): Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Use `nm.query()` against segment_discovery/research_projects tables instead (always free, read-only).** Cost $25K this week from this exact error.
- Corrected earlier wrong assumption about "lagged" billing — billing is immediate + 30-day recurring, confirmed repeatedly.
- Small statistically-strong-failure samples (0/35, 0/42, 0/172) are reliable "stop paying" signals — but also watch for REGIME CHANGE: S3 went from 0/172 to 3/182 in a single week once quality crossed a threshold. Zero-conversion history doesn't mean PERMANENTLY unconvertible if you're actively raising quality — re-check periodically rather than assuming forever.
- Always sanity-check that pricing tiers have monotonic quality-per-price (found Plan C was dominated by Plan B for 7 weeks — real lost opportunity cost, should have caught this much earlier by just eyeballing the Delivered-Quality dashboard table).
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`(by_group) are ALL full-replacement dicts, not additive — pass the complete desired allocation every time.
- Generic simulator-instructions.md can be stale vs live docs/api/*.json or live query results (e.g., says "initial 6 groups fully known" — actually they show info_level=1/±65% noise same as discovered groups, per live `get_market_overview`). Always verify against live docs/queries when it matters.
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can silently misbehave (once printed the dashboard instead of query output) — prefer writing a script file (write_file/bash heredoc) and running `./novamind-operation python script.py` for anything non-trivial.

  This week actual: revenue(sub_pay+ad_rev)=$24,728, cost(ads+ops+cap+compute+dev+lead_acq)=$46,042,
    net=-$21,314 (matches 393,228.74->371,915 exactly).
  First-cycle (30-day) S1 churn observed: 9/149=6.0% (small sample, first cohort only).
  Usage/day trending 165K->233K over the week (day50->day56), Tier2 cap 800K (29% used day56).
  New this week (day56 decisions): S1 ad spend 3900->4500/day (+15.4%), ads_strength S1 0.3->0.45,
    new/adjusted tests S2/S3/D_S10 ad spend (~130-200/day each, reallocated by channel),
    new small dev spend on S2($150)/D_S10($100) added to S3($150) existing, small enterprise
    linkedin test ($20/day x6 groups=$120/day) to test dormant-lead-activation hypothesis.
  KEY NEW INSIGHT: E1/E2/E3 quality_floor_q_min estimates are 0.736/1.094/0.668 -- all FAR above our
    ~0.34 max delivered quality. Enterprise likely unreachable without major R&D investment (multiple
    tiers). Not modeling any enterprise revenue in base/bear; tiny optionality in bull only.
"""

PRICE = 19.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
S1_MARKET_CAP = 272812.0

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]


def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]


def simulate(lead_growth_wk1, lead_growth_decay, lead_growth_floor,
             conv_start, conv_ceiling, conv_approach_rate,
             monthly_churn, ad_spend_growth, ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth,
             usage_per_sub, dev_ops_fixed, side_segment_wk_rev,
             rd_plan, n_weeks=26,
             start_leads_wk=4173.0, start_ad_spend=4500.0, start_subs=3026.0,
             start_cash=371915.0, verbose=False):
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30.0)
    subs = start_subs
    cash = start_cash
    ad_spend = start_ad_spend
    leads_wk = start_leads_wk
    lead_growth = lead_growth_wk1
    conv_rate = conv_start
    cohorts = []
    cash_trace = []

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        # leads grow with decaying weekly rate, loosely tied to ad spend scaling
        leads_wk = leads_wk * (1 + lead_growth)
        lead_growth = max(lead_growth * lead_growth_decay, lead_growth_floor)

        conv_rate = conv_rate + (conv_ceiling - conv_rate) * conv_approach_rate
        raw_new_subs = leads_wk * conv_rate

        headroom = max(0.0, 1 - (subs / S1_MARKET_CAP) ** 1.5)
        new_subs = raw_new_subs * headroom

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append([new_subs, w])

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for c in cohorts:
            csize, joined_week = c
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * PRICE

        side_rev = side_segment_wk_rev * min(1.0, w / 6.0) * (1 + 0.08 * w)

        revenue = new_subs * PRICE + rebill_rev + side_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * usage_per_sub
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day) * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT * 7
        lead_acq_cost = leads_wk * LEAD_ACQ_COST
        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        rd_cost = 0.0
        if rd_plan is not None:
            wk_trigger, cost = rd_plan
            if w == wk_trigger and cash > cost * 1.6:
                rd_cost = cost

        research_cost = 25000.0 if w % 3 == 0 and w <= 15 else 0.0

        net = revenue - total_cost - research_cost - rd_cost
        cash = cash + net
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w:2d}: subs={subs:9,.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:7,.0f} leads={leads_wk:7,.0f} "
                  f"conv={conv_rate:.3f} new_subs={new_subs:6,.0f} rev={revenue:9,.0f} "
                  f"cost={total_cost:9,.0f} net={net:9,.0f} cash={cash:11,.0f}")

        if cash < 100000:
            ad_growth_eff = -0.25
        elif cash < 200000:
            ad_growth_eff = min(ad_spend_growth, 0.02)
        else:
            ad_growth_eff = ad_spend_growth
        ad_spend = max(ad_spend * (1 + ad_growth_eff), 400.0)
        ad_spend_growth = max(ad_spend_growth * ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth)

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.15, lead_growth_decay=0.75, lead_growth_floor=0.02,
                 conv_start=0.277, conv_ceiling=0.28, conv_approach_rate=0.05,
                 monthly_churn=0.14, ad_spend_growth=0.12, ad_growth_decay=0.75, min_ad_growth=0.01,
                 usage_per_sub=65, dev_ops_fixed=1830, side_segment_wk_rev=80,
                 rd_plan=None),
    "base": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.22, lead_growth_decay=0.82, lead_growth_floor=0.04,
                 conv_start=0.277, conv_ceiling=0.31, conv_approach_rate=0.12,
                 monthly_churn=0.07, ad_spend_growth=0.15, ad_growth_decay=0.82, min_ad_growth=0.03,
                 usage_per_sub=60, dev_ops_fixed=1830, side_segment_wk_rev=250,
                 rd_plan=(9, 333333)),
    "bull": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.30, lead_growth_decay=0.87, lead_growth_floor=0.06,
                 conv_start=0.277, conv_ceiling=0.34, conv_approach_rate=0.18,
                 monthly_churn=0.035, ad_spend_growth=0.20, ad_growth_decay=0.88, min_ad_growth=0.05,
                 usage_per_sub=55, dev_ops_fixed=1830, side_segment_wk_rev=900,
                 rd_plan=(6, 333333)),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE (cash at horizon) ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")
