# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory

## 🛑🛑 READ THIS BEFORE CALLING ANY OF: research_market() / research_group() / start_research_project()
**CHECKLIST — go through this EVERY time before invoking one of these three functions:**
1. Have I already called this exact function earlier in THIS session? If yes and I just want to know the outcome → **DO NOT CALL IT AGAIN.** Use `nm.query()` on `segment_discovery` (market/group research) or `research_projects` (R&D) instead — always free, always accurate.
2. These are the ONLY 3 functions in the entire API that charge real money instantly and are easy to accidentally double-invoke "just to check". Every other query-like need should go through `nm.query()`.
3. Made this mistake TWICE already (day49 x2 in one session). Actively re-read this box before touching these 3 functions, not just at the start of the week. **Week8 (day56): called research_market() exactly once this session — clean, no repeat mistake.**

## Game basics (confirmed from live API)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day56, cash $346,914.96** (post wk8 actions incl. one research_market call).
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE at any moment.**
- Billing is IMMEDIATE on signup ($19 Plan A day 1) + recurring every 30 days after (`billing_day_mod30`). Confirmed multiple weeks running.
- Ledger entries for INSTANT actions (market_research, research_group, research_project) post at the CURRENT day, immediately reducing cash BEFORE the next week's simulation runs.
- Enterprise "network"-sourced customer records ALSO incur the $0.5 lead_acquisition_cost even though they never appear in `enterprise_turns` (confirmed via ledger reconciliation day56: 4436 individual leads + 11 enterprise customer creations = 4447 × $0.5 = $2,223.5 ≈ actual $2,224).
- `service_day` table has exact daily usage/capacity/latency/error data — use this (not just the weekly aggregate) to see WITHIN-week trend and spot accelerating usage early.
- Live API doc for `send_enterprise_deal` says **3-day timeout** for no-response ("No response within 3 days = customer LOST FOREVER"), NOT 7 days as the generic instructions state. Trust the live doc; reply same-day regardless if enterprise ever activates.
- R&D: 20 tiers total. T1=$166,667(done,+0.0289 actual), T2=$333,333(mean+0.07,~17d), T3=$500,000(mean+0.11,~23d), T4=$666,667(mean+0.16), T5=$833,333(mean+0.22)... Still holding off T2 — cash too tight relative to $333K cost (would be ~96% of cash right now).
- research_market(): $25K/attempt, ~30% stated chance. Cumulative as of day56: **12 attempts, 6 successes (50%)**. Latest: **D_S04 "Small Agency Teams" discovered day56** — q_min=0.162 (LOW), WTP=$116.36 (HIGH), cap=34,157, usage_vol=215.9. Very promising combo (low bar + high willingness-to-pay) — added small test ad budget. 14 groups remain undiscovered (of 26 total).
- research_group(): Level2=$60K, Level3=$175K, Level4=$350K, Level5=$700K. All groups (incl. initial 6) sit at info_level=1/±65% noise — nobody is "fully known". Not doing any research_group upgrades yet — cash too tight, and empirical small-ad-spend tests are giving useful signal for free.

## ⭐ BIG PICTURE STATUS (day56)
- Individual subs: 1842(day49) → **3026(day56)**, +64.3%/week (decelerating from prior 90.7%, as expected — S1 lead growth rate itself decelerating: wk/wk lead growth 47%,96%,71%,70%,61%,43%,27% for weeks 1-8). This is healthy, expected S-curve behavior, not alarming.
- **S1 conversion still climbing but decelerating: 7.1→6.8→10.0→11.3→17.0→23.7→26.5→27.7% (wk1-8).** Marginal improvement now small (+1.2pp vs +2.8pp prior week) — likely approaching a ceiling around 29-32%. CPL: content $6.61 avg (was $6.51), referral $7.52 avg (was $7.37) — both up slightly, mild saturation signal but not severe.
- **S1 unit economics excellent: CAC ≈ $25-28/customer (blended CPL/conv), first-cycle (30-day) churn measured for the first time: 9/149 = 6.0%** (small sample — first cohort only, most of the 3026 base hasn't hit day-30 yet). If 6%/month churn holds, avg tenure ~17mo, LTV~$300+ >> CAC. Watch this number closely as more cohorts mature (expect 30-day cohort sample to grow a lot over next few weeks).
- **S2 CONVERTED FOR THE FIRST TIME EVER this week: 6/78 leads (7.7%), all via PLAN A (not Plan C!).** Correcting last week's hypothesis: it wasn't the Plan C tier fix that mattered — it's that rising global/group quality bonus pushed **Plan A's** quality just high enough to clear the lower tail of S2's personal quality-bar distribution. Plan C remains 100% unpicked everywhere (0 subscribers on Plan C, ever, across all groups) — not a bug, just means no one's personal bar sits between Plan B and Plan C's delivered quality yet. CAC for S2 ~$140/sub (content channel $98, referral channel $350 — content much better).
- **S3: conversion rate DROPPED from 30%(organic-only) to 10.9% this week (11/101)** now that paid ads are mixed in — expected (paid leads less pre-qualified than organic word-of-mouth). Still net positive: 11 new subs (up from 3), CAC ~$114/sub. **Channel split matters a lot: referral_program converts far better for S3 (15.2%) than content_marketing (4.5%)** — opposite pattern from S2/D_S10. Reallocated budget accordingly (see actions).
- **D_S10: consistent 20% conversion (16/80), CAC ~$52.5/sub — best CAC of all new-segment tests.** content_marketing converts better (18.75%) than referral (20% but noisier/smaller n). Reallocated more budget to content.

Started a cheap ($120/day total, $20/day × 6 groups on linkedin) test to see if ANY ad spend presence activates the 22 dormant leads into negotiation threads — pure optionality, low cost, informative either way. - Ops $700/day: 281 open issues (up from 175), 1,518 resolved this week, resolution time still ~same-day flat (avg days_open ~0.0013) — still huge headroom, no need to increase yet.
- Social media: our posts consistently score **+0.3 to +0.65 with individual segments (S1/S2/S3/D_S07/D_S10)** but **-0.6 to -0.85 with enterprise segments (E1/E2/D_E02/D_E08/D_E09)** every single time we've posted (4 posts so far, all "acknowledging a problem + fix" format). Enterprise reads "acknowledged issues" as operational immaturity red flags; individuals read it as accountability/trustworthy. Given enterprise is likely unreachable on quality grounds anyway (see above), the tradeoff favors continuing this playbook for S1/S2/S3 lead-arrival-speed boosts. Posted a 5th one day56 replying to a support-routing complaint (Jordan/S1).

This likely explains continued enterprise silence; doesn't seem to be hurting individual (S1) conversion so far.

## Week 9 (day56) actions taken
1. **S1 ad spend +15.4%**: content_marketing $2600→$3000/day, referral_program $1300→$1500/day. Unit economics still excellent (CAC $25-28 vs LTV $300+), keep scaling while CPL trend stays mild.
2. **Rebalanced S2/S3/D_S10 ad channel mix** based on this week's per-channel conversion data (see status section): S3 shifted toward referral ($120→$60 content, $60→$140 referral), S2 and D_S10 shifted toward content (S2: $70→$100 content/$50→$30 referral; D_S10: $70→$100 content/$50→$40 referral).
3. **Added D_S04 test budget** (newly discovered, very promising low-q_min/high-WTP combo): $60 content + $40 referral = $100/day.
4. **Enterprise activation test**: linkedin $20/day × 6 groups (E1,E2,E3,D_E02,D_E08,D_E09) = $120/day — testing whether ANY ad spend presence activates the 22 dormant enterprise leads into negotiation threads. Cheap optionality.
5. **ads_strength S1: 0.3→0.45** (effective 0.568→0.703). Prior test at 0.3 was clean (only 5 cancellations out of 3026 subs all week, ad_revenue grew from $230→$803/week). Watch cancellations/satisfaction closely at the new level.
6. **Targeted dev spend: S3 $150 (kept) + S2 $150 (new) + D_S10 $100 (new)** = $400/day total targeted (was $150). Cheap 5x-coefficient quality push for the 3 now-converting side segments. Global dev unchanged $200/day, ops unchanged $700/day.
7. **research_market()** called ONCE — success, discovered D_S04. Cumulative 6/12 successes (50%).
8. **Posted social media reply** (5th post ever, day56) addressing a support-routing complaint from an S1 customer — same playbook that's worked well historically for individual segments.
9. Prices/tiers/quotas/capacity unchanged (A=$19 T2, B=$99 T4, C=$179 T5, quotas 200/280/500, capacity Tier2).
10. Total ad spend now **$5,190/day** (was $4,320, +20.1%). Total daily fixed-ish cost: ads $5,190 + ops $700 + dev $600 + capacity $530 = **$7,020/day**, plus variable compute (~$500-550/day currently, growing) + lead_acq (~$350-400/day, growing).

## R&D strategic thinking
- Tier2 ($333,333) still too large relative to cash ($346,915) — would leave dangerously little buffer (~4% of cash). Holding off again.
- Enterprise quality gap (need ~+0.4 to +0.9 quality points to clear E1/E2/E3 q_min estimates) is FAR bigger than what dev spend alone can close (log-saturation) — would need multiple R&D tiers (T2-T5+, cumulative $2M+) to have a real shot at enterprise. Not worth it until individual-segment cash generation is much stronger. Revisit only after cash comfortably exceeds ~$1-1.5M AND individual growth has matured (mid-game).
- Continue the free/cheap approach for now: targeted dev spend on converting segments (S2/S3/D_S10) + occasional research_market() for new segment discovery. Revisit real R&D tier investment once cash > ~$700K-1M with stable positive cash flow.

## Cost/quality reference (confirmed)
- Model tier cost_per_usage_unit: T1=$0.0003,T2=$0.002,T3=$0.006,T4=$0.012,T5=$0.03/unit. Quality mult: T1=.6,T2=.75,T3=.9,T4=1.0,T5=1.1.
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K/$85/day, T1=200K/$215/day, **T2=800K/$530/day (NOW HERE, 29% utilized day56)**, T3=2.5M/$1330/day, T4=8M/$4000/day, T5=25M/$10K/day, T6=80M/$28K/day, T7=300M/$75K/day.

At Tier2 (800K), supports ~10,400-13,500 subs depending on usage/sub — should last ~3-4 more weeks before needing Tier3. **CHECK `service_day` table WEEKLY, upgrade proactively at ~80% utilization (640K), don't wait for overload flag.**

- Dev quality formula: global `0.0045 × ln(1+global_spend/5000)`/day (permanent), targeted `0.0225 × ln(1+targeted_spend/5000)`/day per group (persists after spend stops, 5x global coefficient). NOTE: observed group-bonus dashboard values didn't visibly change between day49→day56 despite $150/day S3 spend — either the effect is too small to show in 4 decimals over 1 week, or there's a delay; don't over-interpret week-to-week bonus deltas, trust the direction not the precise magnitude.

- Plan C remains unpicked everywhere (0 subscribers ever, any group) even after the T5 tier fix — not a bug, just means quality/price at C doesn't beat A/B for anyone's personal bar yet. Not worth further tuning unless a segment's noisy q_min estimate suggests a gap between B and C specifically.

| Group | content_marketing conv% (CAC) | referral_program conv% (CAC) | Action taken |
|---|---|---|---|

- Sample sizes still small (15-50 leads/channel/group per week) — directional reallocation only, not full commitment. Re-check weekly, don't overfit to single-week noise.

## Forecasting approach
- Model file: `forecast_model_wk8.py` (bear/base/bull scenarios calibrated to day56 actuals: S1 lead/conv history, actual this-week P&L reconciled exactly against ledger). Key mechanic: lead growth rate decaying geometrically (~wk/wk decay 0.75-0.87 depending on scenario) from a wk8 base of 27% growth, conversion rate approaching a ceiling (28-34% depending on scenario) via exponential approach, rebill wave modeled per-cohort every 4 weeks with compounding survivorship.
- Bear scenario has cash trough ~$84-98K around week 6-9, auto-throttles ad spend hard below $100K (built into model), recovers afterward. This matches my actual intended policy (throttle if cash heads toward $100-150K).
- Submitted day56 (for day63/84/140/238): 1wk=$322,000[300K,342K]; 4wk=$192,000[110K,280K]; 12wk=$230,000[60K,550K]; 26wk=$2,100,000[450K,6,000,000].

10. Check `get_social_posts` / macro signals for competitor events — posts increasingly reference PMI contraction (~45.6, described as "below 46") even though official macro table hasn't updated since day1 reading (48.9) — expect an official macro_economic_update notification with a worse reading in the next few weeks (30-day publish lag).
11. Query `predictions` table each week for calibration tracking.
12. **Endgame pivot reminder**: around day450-490, stop chasing new-customer growth (CAC won't pay back), shift to pure cash harvesting (cut ad spend, maximize ads_strength/margin). Not relevant yet at day56.

## Mistakes / lessons log
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Use `nm.query()` against segment_discovery/research_projects tables instead (always free, read-only). Cost $25K once from this error (day49); avoided successfully day56.
- Corrected earlier wrong assumption about "lagged" billing — billing is immediate + 30-day recurring, confirmed repeatedly.
- **Corrected wrong hypothesis from last week**: assumed Plan C's T5 tier fix would be what unlocks S2 conversions. Actual mechanism: rising Plan A quality (from global+group bonuses) crossed the bar for S2's lowest-bar tail — Plan C still has 0 subscribers anywhere. Lesson: don't assume which specific lever caused a change — check which PLAN customers actually picked before attributing causality.

Zero-conversion history doesn't mean PERMANENTLY unconvertible if you're actively raising quality — re-check periodically.

- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`(by_group) are ALL full-replacement dicts, not additive — pass the complete desired allocation every time (confirmed again this week: had to re-call set_targeted_ad_spend a second time within the same session to add D_S04 to the existing allocation, since the first call's dict would otherwise have been replaced/lost the new addition if I'd forgotten to include prior entries).

import novamind_api as nm
import json

print("=== Week 10 (day63) actions ===")

# 1. Ad spend reallocation:
#    - S1: scale winning channels +20% (content 3000->3600, referral 1500->1800),
#      add two NEW exploration channels never tried before (social_media, search_ads
#      $200/day each) to see if there's an even better channel for our best segment.
#    - S2: shift further toward content (clear winner: CAC $117 vs referral $210)
#    - S3: shift further toward referral (proven winner, CAC ~$70, n=98) and increase
#      total budget given excellent economics (WTP $193). Content CAC unproven/noisy (n=18).
#    - D_S10: shift hard toward content (CAC $64 vs referral $280)
#    - D_S04: hold steady, still building sample (first week only, noisy)
#    - linkedin (all 6 enterprise groups): CUT TO ZERO. Confirmed dead: $840 spent this
#      week (6 groups x $140) produced ZERO leads. Combined with 22 dormant enterprise
#      "network" customers producing zero enterprise_turns threads ever, and E1/E2/E3
#      quality floor estimates (0.7-1.1) vastly exceeding our max deliverable quality
#      (~0.34-0.42), enterprise is conclusively unreachable for now. Stop wasting spend.
ad_spend = {
    "content_marketing": {"S1": 3600, "S3": 40, "D_S10": 160, "S2": 140, "D_S04": 60},
    "referral_program": {"S1": 1800, "S3": 220, "D_S10": 10, "S2": 15, "D_S04": 40},
    "social_media": {"S1": 200},
    "search_ads": {"S1": 200},
}
r1 = nm.marketing.set_targeted_ad_spend(targeted_spend=ad_spend)
print("set_targeted_ad_spend -> total/day:", r1.get("total_per_day"))

# 2. ads_strength: S1 0.45 -> 0.55 (gradual increase, still very low cancellation rate:
#    12/4835=0.25% this week vs 5/3026=0.17% last week - small uptick but not alarming
#    given ad_revenue roughly doubled 803->1597/week). Keep other segments at 0 (S2/S3/
#    D_S10 have much tighter quality margins above their bars - too risky to degrade
#    perceived quality there while they're just starting to convert).
r2 = nm.marketing.set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.0, by_group={"S1": 0.55})
print("set_ads_strength ->", r2)

# 3. Targeted dev spend: add S1 (protect our largest revenue base - 4740 subs - against
#    rising customer expectations / competitor events over time; cheap insurance).
#    Increase S2/S3/D_S10 modestly given 5x coefficient is clearly working (group bonuses
#    visibly grew: S2 +0.0491, S3 +0.0685, D_S10 +0.0031).
r3 = nm.analytics.set_targeted_dev_spend(targeted_spend={"S1": 200, "S3": 200, "S2": 180, "D_S10": 130})
print("set_targeted_dev_spend ->", r3)

# 4. ops/global dev unchanged - re-assert explicitly
r4 = nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=700, development=200)
print("set_daily_spend ->", r4)

# 5. Capacity: upgrade Tier2 (800K, $530/day) -> Tier3 (2.5M, $1330/day). Peak usage hit
#    374,409 (46.8% of Tier2 cap) on day63, up from 232,725 (29%) on day56 - usage has
#    been volatile day-to-day (dropped to 208K on day61, spiked to 374K on day63) and
#    subscriber growth (+60% this week) + this week's +23% ad spend increase will keep
#    accelerating lead/usage flow. Proactively upgrading now avoids outage risk (which
#    would cause a widespread quality collapse + reputation cascade far more costly than
#    +$800/day).
r5 = nm.infrastructure.set_capacity_tier(tier=3)
print("set_capacity_tier ->", r5)

# 6. Market research - ONE call only this session (checked MEMORY checklist first!).
r6 = nm.market.research_market()
print("research_market ->", r6)

# 7. Social media reply - Alex Chen (S1, post_id 108) has an unresolved feature issue for
#    a week; same "acknowledge + concrete fix" playbook that's worked repeatedly for
#    individual segments (+0.3 to +0.65 historically). Enterprise reacts negatively but
#    enterprise is confirmed unreachable anyway so the tradeoff still favors S1/individual
#    lead-arrival-speed boosts.
content = ("Alex, a week of silence on a feature issue isn't OK - sorry for the wait. "
           "We've pulled your ticket to the front of the queue and are also rolling out "
           "faster escalation paths this week so this doesn't happen again. Thank you for "
           "your patience.")
print("post length:", len(content))
r7 = nm.marketing.post_social_media(content=content, reply_to_post_id=108)
print("post_social_media ->", r7)

print("\n=== Current cash ===")
r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
print(r["rows"])

    = $9,425/day (was $7,020/day pre-action), +34%.
"""

PRICE = 19.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
S1_MARKET_CAP = 272812.0

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]


def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]


def simulate(lead_growth_wk1, lead_growth_decay, lead_growth_floor,
             conv_start, conv_ceiling, conv_approach_rate,
             monthly_churn, ad_spend_growth, ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth,
             usage_per_sub, dev_ops_fixed, side_segment_wk_rev,
             rd_plan, n_weeks=26,
             start_leads_wk=6139.0, start_ad_spend=6485.0, start_subs=4835.0,
             start_cash=305649.0, verbose=False):
    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30.0)
    subs = start_subs
    cash = start_cash
    ad_spend = start_ad_spend
    leads_wk = start_leads_wk
    lead_growth = lead_growth_wk1
    conv_rate = conv_start
    cohorts = []
    cash_trace = []
    rd_done = False

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):
        leads_wk = leads_wk * (1 + lead_growth)
        lead_growth = max(lead_growth * lead_growth_decay, lead_growth_floor)

        conv_rate = conv_rate + (conv_ceiling - conv_rate) * conv_approach_rate
        raw_new_subs = leads_wk * conv_rate

        headroom = max(0.0, 1 - (subs / S1_MARKET_CAP) ** 1.5)
        new_subs = raw_new_subs * headroom

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs
        cohorts.append([new_subs, w])

        rebill_rev = 0.0
        for c in cohorts:
            csize, joined_week = c
            age_weeks = w - joined_week
            if age_weeks > 0 and age_weeks % 4 == 0:
                survivors = csize * ((1 - weekly_churn) ** age_weeks)
                rebill_rev += survivors * PRICE

        side_rev = side_segment_wk_rev * min(1.0, w / 4.0) * (1 + 0.06 * w)

        revenue = new_subs * PRICE + rebill_rev + side_rev

        ads_cost = ad_spend * 7
        dev_ops_cost = dev_ops_fixed * 7
        usage_per_day = subs * usage_per_sub
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_for(usage_per_day) * 7
        compute_cost = usage_per_day * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT * 7
        lead_acq_cost = leads_wk * LEAD_ACQ_COST
        total_cost = ads_cost + dev_ops_cost + capacity_cost + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost

        rd_cost = 0.0
        if rd_plan is not None and not rd_done:
            min_wk, cost = rd_plan
            if w >= min_wk and cash > cost * 1.8:
                rd_cost = cost
                rd_done = True

        research_cost = 25000.0 if w % 3 == 1 and w <= 21 else 0.0

        net = revenue - total_cost - research_cost - rd_cost
        cash = cash + net
        cash_trace.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{w:2d}: subs={subs:9,.0f} ad_spend={ad_spend:7,.0f} leads={leads_wk:7,.0f} "
                  f"conv={conv_rate:.3f} new_subs={new_subs:6,.0f} rev={revenue:9,.0f} "
                  f"cost={total_cost:9,.0f} net={net:9,.0f} cash={cash:11,.0f}")

        if cash < 100000:
            ad_growth_eff = -0.30
        elif cash < 200000:
            ad_growth_eff = min(ad_spend_growth, 0.02)
        else:
            ad_growth_eff = ad_spend_growth
        ad_spend = max(ad_spend * (1 + ad_growth_eff), 400.0)
        ad_spend_growth = max(ad_spend_growth * ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth)

    return cash_trace


scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.08, lead_growth_decay=0.70, lead_growth_floor=0.01,
                 conv_start=0.288, conv_ceiling=0.29, conv_approach_rate=0.05,
                 monthly_churn=0.15, ad_spend_growth=0.10, ad_growth_decay=0.70, min_ad_growth=0.01,
                 usage_per_sub=68, dev_ops_fixed=2940, side_segment_wk_rev=100,
                 rd_plan=None),
    "base": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.20, lead_growth_decay=0.80, lead_growth_floor=0.03,
                 conv_start=0.288, conv_ceiling=0.32, conv_approach_rate=0.10,
                 monthly_churn=0.08, ad_spend_growth=0.14, ad_growth_decay=0.80, min_ad_growth=0.03,
                 usage_per_sub=63, dev_ops_fixed=2940, side_segment_wk_rev=300,
                 rd_plan=(6, 333333)),
    "bull": dict(lead_growth_wk1=0.32, lead_growth_decay=0.87, lead_growth_floor=0.05,
                 conv_start=0.288, conv_ceiling=0.35, conv_approach_rate=0.16,
                 monthly_churn=0.04, ad_spend_growth=0.18, ad_growth_decay=0.87, min_ad_growth=0.05,
                 usage_per_sub=58, dev_ops_fixed=2940, side_segment_wk_rev=1000,
                 rd_plan=(4, 333333)),
}

horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    print(f"\n--- {name} scenario ---")
    trace = simulate(**params, n_weeks=26, verbose=True)
    results[name] = trace

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY TABLE (cash at horizon) ===")
for hname, hweek in horizons.items():
    vals = [results[s][hweek - 1] for s in scenarios]
    print(f"{hname}: bear={vals[0]:,.0f} base={vals[1]:,.0f} bull={vals[2]:,.0f}")

Use `nm.query()` against segment_discovery/research_projects tables instead (always free, read-only). Cost $25K once from this error (day49); clean since then (day56, day63).
- **Forecast modeling lesson (day63)**: don't forget to credit the EXISTING subscriber base's ongoing MRR rebill in near-term cash forecasts — a model that only tracks new-cohort rebills understates week 1-4 revenue substantially. - **Strategy lesson (day63)**: be careful about stacking MULTIPLE simultaneous cost increases (ads +23%, dev +78%, capacity +151%) in the same week — even when each individually looks justified, the COMBINED effect on near-term cash runway can create an uncomfortable trough that's easy to miss if you only look at each decision in isolation.     stacked increase, given the trough-risk lesson learned.
"""

PRICE = 19.34  # blended ARPU per sub (MRR/subs)

CAP_TIERS = [
    (50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
    (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000),
]


def cap_cost_for(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAP_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAP_TIERS[-1][1]

             conv_start, conv_ceiling, conv_approach_rate,
             monthly_churn, ad_spend_growth, ad_growth_decay, min_ad_growth,

    fixed_cost = fixed_cost_wk

    for w in range(1, n_weeks + 1):

        lead_growth = max(lead_growth * lead_growth_decay, lead_growth_floor)

        conv_rate = conv_rate + (conv_ceiling - conv_rate) * conv_approach_rate
        new_subs = leads_wk * conv_rate

        churned = subs * weekly_churn
        subs = subs - churned + new_subs

        # revenue: new signups pay immediately (~PRICE), existing MRR base rebills
        # continuously (approximated as even weekly draw at MRR/4.3, decaying with churn)
        new_signup_rev = new_subs * PRICE
        mrr_now = subs * PRICE

import json

print("=== WEEK 11 (day70) ACTIONS ===")

# 1. Ad spend: +15% overall, reallocated toward best-CAC channels based on
#    day64-70 per-channel data (2-week views where noted).
#    S1: content_marketing (best CAC $19.6) and referral (CAC $27) both scaled up.
#         social_media/search_ads (new channels, conv~27% similar to content but
#         CPL 3x higher) scaled up modestly to keep gathering data.
#    S2: content clearly better (CAC $65-91) than referral (CAC $105-210, tiny n) -> shift more to content.
#    S3: 2-week CAC shows content ($82.86) actually BETTER than referral ($111.1,
#        which has gotten worse vs 2wks ago) -> shift some budget back to content.
#    D_S10: referral produced ZERO leads this week at $10/day -> cut to 0, add to content.
#    D_S04: referral CAC ($186.67) better than content ($280) over 2wks -> shift slightly to referral.
ad_spend = {
    "content_marketing": {"S1": 4200, "S2": 180, "S3": 70, "D_S10": 200, "D_S04": 50},
    "referral_program": {"S1": 2000, "S2": 5, "S3": 180, "D_S04": 70},
    "social_media": {"S1": 250},
    "search_ads": {"S1": 250},
}
r = nm.marketing.set_targeted_ad_spend(targeted_spend=ad_spend)
print("set_targeted_ad_spend:", json.dumps(r))
total_ad = sum(sum(v.values()) for v in ad_spend.values())
print("Total ad spend/day:", total_ad, "(was 6485, +{:.1f}%)".format((total_ad/6485-1)*100))

# 2. ads_strength: HOLD at S1=0.55 (no change) this week -- social media showed a
#    "nickel-and-dimed" complaint (post 129) that may partly reflect in-app ad load;
#    don't stack another increase on top of ad spend + ops + dev increases this week.
r = nm.marketing.set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.0, by_group={"S1": 0.55})
print("set_ads_strength (unchanged):", json.dumps(r))

# 3. Ops spend: $700 -> $850/day. Issue volume growing fast (609/day now vs ~380/day
#    3wks ago), resolution time creeping up (0.014d -> 0.42d avg this week), and social
#    media has visible complaints about tickets "vanishing"/no response. Still well
#    under the 2-day quality threshold, but cheap to stay ahead of it before it snowballs.
# Global dev: keep $200/day.
r = nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=850, development=200)
print("set_daily_spend:", json.dumps(r))

# 4. Targeted dev spend: raise across the board proportional to subscriber growth,
#    add D_S04 (previously $0, weak conversion for 2 weeks -- worth testing whether a
#    quality bump unlocks the regime-change pattern seen before in S2/S3/D_S10).
dev_spend = {"S1": 280, "S2": 200, "S3": 220, "D_S10": 150, "D_S04": 80}
r = nm.marketing.set_targeted_dev_spend(targeted_spend=dev_spend)

# 5. Usage quotas: raise Plan A 200->230. D_S04 estimated usage_volume (215.9) exceeds
#    the current 200 quota, likely causing overage-degraded experience that hurts
#    conversion; most other groups avg ~73-82 units/day so this mostly helps the tail

print("set_usage_quotas:", json.dumps(r))

# 6. Capacity: HOLD Tier 3 (peak usage 555,042/day = 22.2% of 2.5M cap -- huge headroom).
# 7. Prices/tiers/promotions: HOLD (working well, Plan C now has 4 S3 subscribers).

# 8. Market research: one attempt this week (first this session).
res = nm.market.research_market()
print("research_market:", json.dumps(res))

# 9. Social media: reply to Jordan Taylor's pricing/value complaint (post 129) --

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory

## 🛑🛑 READ THIS BEFORE CALLING ANY OF: research_market() / research_group() / start_research_project()
**CHECKLIST — go through this EVERY time before invoking one of these three functions:**
1. Have I already called this exact function earlier in THIS session? If yes and I just want to know the outcome → **DO NOT CALL IT AGAIN.** Use `nm.query()` on `segment_discovery` (market/group research) or `research_projects` (R&D) instead — always free, always accurate.
2. These are the ONLY 3 functions in the entire API that charge real money instantly and are easy to accidentally double-invoke "just to check". Every other query-like need should go through `nm.query()`.
3. Track record: made this mistake twice on day49 (fixed cost $25K). Clean (no repeat) on day56, day63, day70. Keep re-reading this box every week before touching these 3 functions.

## Game basics (confirmed from live API)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000.
- **Currently day70, cash $253,548.40** (post wk11 actions incl. one research_market call this session — unsuccessful, 14th attempt, 6/14=42.9% cumulative success rate).
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE at any moment.**
- Timing convention CONFIRMED precisely this week: actions taken during the "Day X dashboard" session apply starting day X+1 through day X+7 (i.e., the NEXT 7 days), shown at the "Day X+7 dashboard". Day X itself still reflects the PRIOR week's config. Verified via ad_channel_leads day-by-day spend transition exactly at day63->64.
- Billing is IMMEDIATE on signup + recurring every 30 days after (`billing_day_mod30`). Confirmed many weeks running.
- **Rebill dynamics — IMPORTANT for forecasting**: subscription_payment revenue each week = (new signups × price) + (rebills from cohorts hitting their 30-day mark). Because the subscriber base grew explosively only in the last ~5-6 weeks, MOST of the base is still <30 days old, so near-term rebill revenue is much smaller than "MRR/4.3 per week" would suggest (that naive ratio wildly overstates near-term rebill since it assumes an already-mature, evenly-aged base). Got an `AttributeError` this week from assuming it was in marketing — wasted one script run (no cash cost, just wasted a call). Double check module namespacing against the instructions/docs before scripting: pricing/marketing/infrastructure/enterprise/market/research/analytics all have DIFFERENT functions, don't assume.
- **Forecast modeling lesson (day70)**: a "smoothed legacy MRR/4.3 per week" rebill approximation OVERSTATES near-term revenue when the subscriber base is mostly young (<30 days old) — most of a hypergrowth cohort hasn't hit its first billing evaluation yet. Use the ACTUAL tenure histogram (`(current_day-start_day)` distribution) to seed an explicit cohort-based model instead — much more accurate, and available for free via `nm.query()` on `subscriptions.start_day`.

Shaded this week's forecasts up modestly (+5-10%) and widened upper bounds more than lower bounds to correct for this recurring optimistic-surprise pattern. Re-check next week whether this correction was appropriate or overcorrected.
- Strategy lesson (day63, still valid): avoid stacking MULTIPLE simultaneous large cost increases in the same week. This week deliberately kept the combined increase moderate (+14.2% vs last week's +34%) as a direct application of that lesson.
- Enterprise: conclusively dead (direct zero-lead test in prior weeks). Don't re-test.
- Small statistically-strong-failure samples are reliable "stop paying" signals (e.g. D_S10 referral 0/many leads this week) — but watch for regime changes on longer timescales; re-check periodically rather than assuming permanence (except enterprise, where the quality gap is well-quantified and too large).
- Always sanity-check that pricing tiers have monotonic quality-per-price (Plan C dominated by Plan B for 7 weeks previously until a promotion fixed net-price ordering — now working, 4 S3 subscribers).
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`(by_group) are ALL full-replacement dicts, not additive — pass the complete desired allocation every time; omitting a key zeros it out (confirmed again: omitted "linkedin" and D_S10-referral entirely this week to zero them).
- Generic simulator-instructions.md can be stale vs live docs/api/*.json (e.g., R&D has 20 tiers not 10; post_social_media limit is "1/day" not "1/week"). Always verify against live docs/queries when it matters.

"""
Week 12 (day77) crisis forecast model.
Context: 4 competitor events (day69-72) raised customer quality expectations by
a combined ~0.3+ (huge). New-lead conversion cratered from ~27-30% to ~5% (S1) and
~0-2% (S2/S3/D_S04/D_S10) starting exactly day70. Cash burn spiked to -$62K/week.
Action: slashing ad spend ~77% + testing lead promotions to recover conversion +
skipping discretionary spend (research_market) to preserve cash.

This model: cohort/mod30-bucket based revenue projection + scenario-based new
signup/churn assumptions (bear/base/bull) to produce 1/4/12/26wk cash forecasts.
"""
import novamind_api as nm

CURRENT_DAY = 77
CASH_NOW = 191540.0
ARPU = 19.32  # blended monthly revenue per active sub (MRR/subs)

# Get current mod30 billing bucket histogram (count, revenue-if-billed)
r = nm.query('''
SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(effective_price) as rev
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30
''')
buckets = {row['billing_day_mod30']: [row['n'], row['rev']] for row in r['rows']}
for i in range(30):
    if i not in buckets:
        buckets[i] = [0, 0.0]

def run_scenario(weekly_new_signups, monthly_churn_rate, ad_spend_wk, other_cost_wk, weeks=26):
    """Simulate forward `weeks` weeks; returns list of end-of-week cash values."""
    b = {k: list(v) for k, v in buckets.items()}
    cash = CASH_NOW
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    cash_by_week = []
    for wk in range(weeks):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        for _ in range(7):
            day += 1
            m = day % 30
            n, rev = b[m]
            if n > 0:
                week_revenue += rev
                # churn applied to this bucket (they just faced re-evaluation)
                survive = 1 - monthly_churn_rate
                b[m][0] = n * survive
                b[m][1] = rev * survive
            # new signups distributed to today's bucket (spread evenly across week)
            new_n = weekly_new_signups / 7.0
            new_rev = new_n * ARPU
            b[m][0] += new_n
            b[m][1] += new_rev
        # new signup revenue collected immediately (already counted turn above as part of bucket add?
        # No - bucket add doesn't bill immediately, so add new signup revenue explicitly this week:
        new_signup_revenue = weekly_new_signups * ARPU
        ad_rev = 430 * 7  # roughly flat, small
        total_revenue = week_revenue + new_signup_revenue + ad_rev
        total_cost = ad_spend_wk + other_cost_wk
        cash += total_revenue - total_cost
        cash_by_week.append(cash)
    return cash_by_week

scenarios = {
    'bear': dict(weekly_new_signups=100, monthly_churn_rate=0.16, ad_spend_wk=10000, other_cost_wk=24000),
    'base': dict(weekly_new_signups=230, monthly_churn_rate=0.10, ad_spend_wk=13000, other_cost_wk=23000),
    'bull': dict(weekly_new_signups=450, monthly_churn_rate=0.08, ad_spend_wk=20000, other_cost_wk=23000),
}

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    cash_series = run_scenario(**params)
    results[name] = cash_series
    print(f"{name}: wk1={cash_series[0]:,.0f} wk4={cash_series[3]:,.0f} wk12={cash_series[11]:,.0f} wk26={cash_series[25]:,.0f}")

print()
print("Full base scenario weekly cash trajectory:")
for i, c in enumerate(results['base']):
    print(f"  week{i+1} (day{CURRENT_DAY+7*(i+1)}): {c:,.0f}")

## 🚨🚨 CRISIS DECLARED DAY70-77: COMPETITOR-DRIVEN QUALITY GAP CRUSHED CONVERSION 🚨🚨
**THIS IS THE #1 THING TO UNDERSTAND. Read this before anything else below.**
- Between day69-72, **FOUR separate competitor events** hit simultaneously (visible via `get_social_posts`, search for "quality boost"/"quality bump"): day69 +0.0914, day70 +0.1031, day71 +0.0943, day72 +0.0771. - Our OWN delivered quality barely moved that week (0.2442→0.2471 for S1 Plan A, i.e. +0.003 from routine dev spend) — utterly dwarfed by the expectation jump. Per game mechanics, these expectation shifts are **PERMANENT** — only offset-able via dev spend (slow, log-saturating) or R&D (expensive, but the only lever that can make jumps this large).
- **Result: new-lead conversion collapsed practically overnight.** Day68-69 S1 conversion was ~30-33%. Day70 onward: ~3.7-6.2%. Verified this is exactly synchronized with the competitor-event timing (not a gradual drift). Same collapse seen in S2 (11.5%→1.2%), S3 (14.6%→0%), D_S04 (3.8%→1.0%), D_S10 (14.0%→1.9%).

Net cash burn spiked from -$27,101/wk (day63-70) to **-$62,008/wk** (day70-77) despite continued subscriber growth (6802→7177), because we kept spending at the OLD ad budget ($52,185/wk) into a funnel that had just become 5x less efficient.

1. **Watch whether lead_promotion ($8/mo, S1/S2/D_S04/D_S10) recovers conversion at all next week.** Query the same conversion-by-created_day breakdown (see script pattern below) each week. 2. **Watch the day48-56 cohort's 30-day billing evaluation (hits day78-86)** — this is the FIRST cohort to be **fully** exposed to the new post-event expectations at their evaluation (day41-47 cohort this week was only partially exposed since events landed right at the start of their eval week). Given the gap is ~0.3+, may need 2-3 tiers over time to meaningfully close it — treat this as a marathon, start as soon as affordable rather than waiting for "comfortable" cash levels, since competitor events will likely keep recurring and compounding the gap.
4. Don't panic-cut further unless cash drops below ~$120-150K with no sign of stabilizing — the crisis-mode ad spend cut should already flip weekly burn from -$62K to roughly -$10K to -$15K range. Reassess with real day84 data before cutting deeper or re-expanding.

- `forecast_model_wk12_crisis.py`: seeds current `billing_day_mod30` histogram (count + revenue-if-billed per bucket), simulates forward day-by-day applying: (a) rebill + monthly-churn-rate-based attrition when a bucket's mod30 matches the current day, (b) new signups added daily split across the mod30 cycle, (c) fixed weekly cost assumptions (ads/capacity/compute/dev/ops/lead_acq). ## Mistakes / lessons log
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Cost $25K once (day49); clean since.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend` lives in `nm.analytics`, NOT `nm.marketing`. `set_targeted_ad_spend` and `set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength` ARE in `nm.marketing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) also in `nm.marketing`.
- **BIG LESSON (day77): a single week can completely invalidate the prior week's spending plan.** Had been running a smooth "increase spend ~15%/week, moderate" playbook for weeks; a competitor-event shock made that OLD plan (unchanged from day70) burn -$62K in one week because ad spend kept flowing into a funnel that had just silently become 5x less efficient. **Takeaway: always re-verify conversion rate (leads→subscribers) each week before assuming last week's ad spend allocation is still efficient — don't just look at subscriber COUNT growth (which lags/can mask a conversion collapse for a week if driven by prior-week's leads still converting).** Check `customers.created_day` vs `subscriptions.status` conversion EVERY week going forward as a standard health check, not just when something looks wrong.
- **Forecast lesson (day77): a 1-week-ahead forecast missed its CI by ~18% because of an unforecastable competitor event that landed the day after submission.** Don't over-tighten near-term CIs just because recent weeks were stable — exogenous shocks can hit any week. Keep at least ~10-15% width on 1wk CIs even in "calm" periods, more once already in a volatile regime.
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`(by_group) are ALL full-replacement dicts, not additive — pass the complete desired allocation every time; omitting a key zeros it out.
- Competitor events are NOT random flavor text — they cite specific quality-boost magnitudes that appear to be literal, and can cluster (4 events in 4 days here). Monitor `get_social_posts` weekly specifically for these, not just for direct customer sentiment.
- Cohort-based revenue modeling (via `billing_day_mod30` bucket histogram) is far more accurate than smoothed MRR/4.3-type approximations — the bucket populations are NOT uniform when growth has been lumpy, causing real week-to-week revenue swings unrelated to underlying health. Always pull the live histogram before forecasting.
- Generic simulator-instructions.md can be stale vs live docs/api/*.json (e.g., R&D has 20 tiers not 10). Always verify against live docs/queries when it matters.
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can occasionally misbehave. Prefer writing a script file and running `./novamind-operation python script.py` for anything non-trivial.

import novamind_api as nm

# Pull current state
cash_now = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as c FROM ledger")['rows'][0]['c']
hist = nm.query("""SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) n, AVG(effective_price) avgp
                    FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30""")['rows']
current_day = nm.vars.current_day
print("cash_now", cash_now, "day", current_day)

buckets = {row['billing_day_mod30']: [row['n'], row['avgp']] for row in hist}
total_subs = sum(v[0] for v in buckets.values())
print("total_subs", total_subs)

# Weekly fixed costs (new config as of day84 actions)
ADS = 2000.0          # per day
OPS = 1100.0
DEV_GLOBAL = 220.0
DEV_TARGETED = 380+205+230+160+80  # 1055
CAPACITY = 1330.0     # tier3 fixed daily
COMPUTE_PER_SUB_DAY = 8413.938/7/7344  # rough $/sub/day compute cost basis this week

def simulate(days, weekly_new_signups, monthly_churn_rate, avg_new_price=15.0, label=""):
    b = {k: list(v) for k, v in buckets.items()}
    cash = cash_now
    daily_new = weekly_new_signups/7.0
    day = current_day
    cash_trace = []
    for d in range(1, days+1):
        day += 1
        mod = day % 30
        # billing event for this bucket
        if mod in b:
            n, avgp = b[mod]
            churned = n*monthly_churn_rate
            n_after = n - churned
            revenue = n*avgp  # everyone in bucket bills at current avg price (churn decided at billing, still pay this cycle in most models -> but to be conservative assume churned ones don't pay)
            revenue = n_after*avgp  # only survivors pay (conservative - matches "evaluate then decide" for renewal)
            b[mod][0] = n_after
        else:
            revenue = 0.0
        # new signups added to today's bucket (their first payment happens immediately)
        new_n = daily_new
        new_revenue = new_n*avg_new_price
        if mod in b:
            old_n, old_avg = b[mod]
            tot = old_n+new_n
            blended = (old_n*old_avg + new_n*19.0)/tot if tot>0 else old_avg
            b[mod] = [tot, blended]
        # costs
        subs_now = sum(v[0] for v in b.values())
        compute = subs_now*COMPUTE_PER_SUB_DAY
        ad_rev = subs_now*0.42  # ~ $3111/week/7344subs/7days = 0.0605/sub/day -> recompute below properly
        daily_cost = ADS+OPS+DEV_GLOBAL+DEV_TARGETED+CAPACITY+compute + (daily_new/0.18)*0.5
        daily_rev = revenue+new_revenue+ad_rev
        cash += daily_rev - daily_cost
        cash_trace.append(cash)
    return cash_trace

# calibrate ad_rev per sub properly: 3110.66/7 days /7344 subs
AD_REV_PER_SUB_DAY = 3110.6557655069473/7/7344

def simulate2(days, weekly_new_signups, monthly_churn_rate, conv_rate=0.18, avg_new_first_price=14.0, label=""):
    b = {k: list(v) for k, v in buckets.items()}
    cash = cash_now
    daily_new = weekly_new_signups/7.0
    day = current_day
    trace = {}
    for d in range(1, days+1):
        day += 1
        mod = day % 30
        revenue = 0.0
        if mod in b:
            n, avgp = b[mod]
            n_after = n*(1-monthly_churn_rate)
            revenue = n_after*avgp
            b[mod][0] = n_after
        new_n = daily_new
        new_revenue = new_n*avg_new_first_price
        if mod in b:
            old_n, old_avg = b[mod]
            tot = old_n+new_n
            blended = (old_n*old_avg + new_n*19.0)/tot if tot>0 else old_avg
            b[mod] = [tot, blended]
        subs_now = sum(v[0] for v in b.values())
        compute = subs_now*COMPUTE_PER_SUB_DAY
        ad_rev = subs_now*AD_REV_PER_SUB_DAY
        leads = daily_new/conv_rate
        daily_cost = ADS+OPS+DEV_GLOBAL+DEV_TARGETED+CAPACITY+compute + leads*0.5
        daily_rev = revenue+new_revenue+ad_rev
        cash += daily_rev-daily_cost
        if d in (7,28,84,182):
            trace[d] = (cash, subs_now)
    return trace

print()
print("=== Scenario runs ===")
scenarios = {
    "bear": dict(weekly_new_signups=450, monthly_churn_rate=0.17, conv_rate=0.14),
    "base": dict(weekly_new_signups=650, monthly_churn_rate=0.14, conv_rate=0.18),
    "bull": dict(weekly_new_signups=850, monthly_churn_rate=0.10, conv_rate=0.20),
}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    tr = simulate2(182, **params)
    print(name, params)
    for d,(c,s) in tr.items():
        print(f"   day+{d}: cash={c:,.0f} subs={s:,.0f}")

Always verify against live docs/queries when it matters.
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can occasionally misbehave. Prefer writing a script file and running `./novamind-operation python script.py` for anything non-trivial.

- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Cost $25K once (day49); clean since.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend` lives in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`.
- **`set_promotion` (recurring, every billing) vs `set_lead_promotion` (first-bill-only)**: not interchangeable; use `set_promotion` for retention, `set_lead_promotion` for conversion. Tested the S1 $2 ongoing promo starting day85 — **no clean evidence yet it's helping retention** (churn kept rising through evaluations that had it fully active); keeping it another 2-3 weeks before concluding, since there's no counterfactual and the underlying trend may simply be worsening faster than $2 can offset.
- **BIG LESSON (reconfirmed day91): always analyze churn by cohort `start_day` (when did the eventual-canceller sign up), broken into weekly or even daily buckets, not just aggregate weekly cancellation counts** — the trend WITHIN a supposedly-uniform pre-crisis cohort window (start_day 49-61) is itself climbing (11.7%→32.2%), which would be invisible if you just looked at "elevated churn ~16-22%" as a single flat number. Always check the within-cohort trend, not just the average.
- **`get_social_posts()` API's `days` parameter is unreliable for restricting to recent posts** — it returned posts from day 7 through day91 despite `days=7`. Prefer direct SQL: `nm.query("SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE day > X ORDER BY day")`. Note the `social_media_posts` table only has columns `post_id, day, content` (no group_id, despite the API doc implying richer fields — those are presumably synthesized server-side in `get_social_posts`'s formatted output, not in the raw table).
- **Forecast lesson (day91): when raw cohort data shows churn on a WORSENING trend (not flat), a single-flat-rate scenario model runs slightly optimistic** — shade point estimates down within the bear/base/bull band rather than trusting "base" at face value. Applied this day91 (blended ~40/40/20 bear/base/bull instead of pure base).
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`(by_group) are ALL full-replacement dicts — pass the complete desired allocation every time; omitting a key zeros it out.
- Competitor events cite specific quality-boost magnitudes, appear literal, and can cluster (4 events in 4 days seen once). Monitor weekly via direct SQL on `social_media_posts`.
- Generic simulator-instructions.md can be stale/imprecise vs live docs/api/*.json — always verify against live docs/queries when it matters.
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can occasionally misbehave. Prefer writing a script file and running `./novamind-operation python script.py` for anything non-trivial.

import novamind_api as nm

cash_now = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as c FROM ledger")['rows'][0]['c']
current_day = nm.vars.current_day
print("cash_now", cash_now, "day", current_day)

hist = nm.query("""SELECT start_day, COUNT(*) n, AVG(effective_price) avgp
                    FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY start_day""")['rows']

# Build cohort list: [start_day, count, avg_price, evals_passed, next_eval_day]
cohorts = []
for row in hist:
    sd, n, avgp = row['start_day'], row['n'], row['avgp']
    evals_passed = (current_day - sd) // 30
    next_eval = sd + 30 * (evals_passed + 1)
    cohorts.append([sd, float(n), avgp, evals_passed, next_eval])

total0 = sum(c[1] for c in cohorts)
print("total active now:", total0)

# New (post-crisis, day92-98 actions) cost structure
OPS = 900.0
DEV_GLOBAL = 235.0
DEV_TARGETED_S1 = 550.0   # cut S2/S3/D_S10/D_S04 targeting to 0
ADS = 0.0                 # cut essentially to zero (was $2000/day)
CAPACITY = 1330.0
COMPUTE_PER_SUB_DAY = 8525.832/7/7097.5   # recalibrated day92-98
AD_REV_PER_SUB_DAY = 3041.40/7/7097.5
NEW_SIGNUP_PRICE = 17.5   # ~ list 19 minus small promo/lead-promo effects

FIXED_DAILY = ADS+OPS+DEV_GLOBAL+DEV_TARGETED_S1+CAPACITY
print("FIXED_DAILY (ex compute/lead_acq):", FIXED_DAILY, " weekly:", FIXED_DAILY*7)

def simulate(days, weekly_new_signups, first_eval_churn, repeat_eval_churn, label=""):
    cohs = [list(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash_now
    day = current_day
    trace = {}
    base_leads_per_week = 750.0   # organic/network leads at current sub level
    for d in range(1, days+1):
        day += 1
        revenue = 0.0
        for c in cohs:
            sd, n, avgp, evals_passed, next_eval = c
            if day == next_eval and n > 0.5:
                rate = first_eval_churn if evals_passed == 0 else repeat_eval_churn
                survivors = n * (1 - rate)
                revenue += survivors * avgp
                c[1] = survivors
                c[3] = evals_passed + 1
                c[4] = next_eval + 30
        # new signups (spread daily)
        new_n = weekly_new_signups/7.0
        cohs.append([day, new_n, NEW_SIGNUP_PRICE, 0, day+30])
        # they pay immediately on signup (billing immediate)
        revenue += new_n*NEW_SIGNUP_PRICE

        subs_now = sum(c[1] for c in cohs)
        scale = subs_now/total0 if total0>0 else 1.0
        compute = subs_now*COMPUTE_PER_SUB_DAY
        ad_rev = subs_now*AD_REV_PER_SUB_DAY
        leads_today = (base_leads_per_week*scale)/7.0
        lead_cost = leads_today*0.5
        daily_cost = ADS+OPS+DEV_GLOBAL+DEV_TARGETED_S1+CAPACITY+compute+lead_cost
        daily_rev = revenue+ad_rev
        cash += daily_rev - daily_cost
        if d in (7,28,84,182):
            trace[d] = (cash, subs_now)
    return trace

print()
print("=== CRISIS Scenario runs (day98, post competitor-shock cluster day92-95) ===")
scenarios = {
    "bear (persistent ~55%/45% churn, low signups)":
        dict(weekly_new_signups=60, first_eval_churn=0.58, repeat_eval_churn=0.45),
    "base (one-time catchup ~45%, then stabilizes ~22%)":
        dict(weekly_new_signups=100, first_eval_churn=0.45, repeat_eval_churn=0.22),
    "bull (fast stabilization ~32%/15%)":
        dict(weekly_new_signups=150, first_eval_churn=0.32, repeat_eval_churn=0.15),
}
results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    trace = simulate(182, **params)
    print(name, params)
    for d, (cash, subs) in trace.items():
        print(f"  day+{d}: cash={cash:,.0f} subs={subs:,.0f}")
    results[name] = trace

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory (updated day98)

## 🛑🛑 READ THIS BEFORE CALLING ANY OF: research_market() / research_group() / start_research_project()
**CHECKLIST — go through this EVERY time before invoking one of these three functions:**
1. Have I already called this exact function earlier in THIS session? If yes and I just want to know the outcome → **DO NOT CALL IT AGAIN.** Use `nm.query()` on `segment_discovery` (market/group research) or `research_projects` (R&D) instead — always free, always accurate.
2. These are the ONLY 3 functions in the entire API that charge real money instantly and are easy to accidentally double-invoke "just to check". Every other query-like need should go through `nm.query()`.
3. Track record: made this mistake twice on day49 (fixed cost $25K). Clean since. R&D/research_market SKIPPED continuously since day70 (day70,77,84,91,98 — 5 weeks running) for cash preservation. Given the crisis (see below), continue skipping indefinitely until cash is stable and clearly recovering.

## 🚨🚨🚨 SEVERE CRISIS AS OF DAY98 — MASSIVE COMPETITOR SHOCK CLUSTER (day92-95) BROKE THE FUNNEL
**Read this before anything else. This is a bigger crisis than the day84-91 one.**

### What happened
- **Day92-95: a MUCH bigger competitor-event cluster hit than the previous one** (day69-72 cluster was +0.09-0.10 each). New cluster: day92 CloudPeak/QuantumEdge +0.1278, day93 RivalTech/CloudPeak +0.1374, day94 CloudPeak/NexGen +0.1665, day95 RivalTech/NexGen +0.1331. **Each day's TWO differently-named-competitor posts cite the IDENTICAL magnitude — strong evidence it's really ONE event/day with 2 flavor-text posts, i.e. 4 real events, cumulative ~+0.56 raw (before per-group sensitivity scaling).** This permanently raised customer expected quality across groups (unevenly — some groups more trend-sensitive than others, per game design).
- **Result: conversion rate for NEW leads collapsed from 20.8% (day91) to 5.2% (S1, day98), ~4.9% overall.** This is NOT channel-specific — paid (content_marketing 5.0%, referral 5.3%) and organic/"network" (5.6%) all converts at the SAME ~5% rate now. Confirms: the bottleneck is the quality-expectation gap, not targeting/channel choice.
- **Result: cohort churn at 30-day evaluation went from ~20-32% (already elevated, day84-91 read) to 54.9%-61.7%** for cohorts (start_day 63-68) whose 30-day evaluation fell in the day93-98 window — i.e., they signed up BEFORE the shock (expecting the old, lower bar) and got re-evaluated against the massively-higher new bar. This drove 1,294 cancellations this week (vs 404 last week), subscriber base fell from 7,662→**6,533 (-14.7%)**.
- **Cash burn this week: -$24,599** (cash $160,727→$136,128). Revenue (sub_pay+ad_rev) $26,846 vs cost $51,446 (ads $14,000 + dev $10,220 + capacity $9,310 + compute $8,526 + ops $7,700 + lead_acq $1,690).

### 🔑 KEY MECHANIC INSIGHT (new understanding — cohort "reckoning" is a ONE-TIME TRANSITION EVENT, not a permanently-elevated per-eval rate)
Churn isn't "everyone now churns at 55% forever." Rather: **each individual subscriber faces ONE reckoning evaluation** — the first 30-day billing evaluation that occurs AFTER a permanent expectation-raising shock happened during their subscription. Subscribers who signed up BEFORE day92 and haven't yet had a post-day95 evaluation are all queued for this one-time reckoning at their own next 30-day mark (spread across start_day, arriving in waves over the next ~3-4 weeks: cohorts w/ next-eval day99-105 ≈1,260 people [start_day 39-45 2nd-eval + 69-75 1st-eval], day106-112 another ~1,200-1,300, etc., tapering off by ~day121-128 once all pre-shock cohorts have passed through). **AFTER a customer survives (or churns at) this one reckoning, subsequent evaluations should reflect only ambient drift** (much lower churn, if no NEW competitor cluster occurs) — but we have NO confirmed data on this yet (too early). This is the single biggest unknown driving forecast uncertainty. **Watch closely over the next 3-4 weeks**: query cohort churn by start_day each week (script below) — if 2nd+/repeat evaluations (for cohorts that already had 1 eval survive) show much LOWER churn than the ~55-62% first-reckoning rate, that confirms the "one-time transition" theory and the crisis is temporary/self-resolving. If repeat evaluations STAY elevated (40%+), the crisis is structural/persistent and far more dangerous.

### Cohort churn data (query for reference, re-run to extend):
```sql
SELECT start_day, SUM(CASE WHEN status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active, COUNT(*) total
FROM subscriptions WHERE start_day BETWEEN <X> AND <Y> AND status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
GROUP BY start_day ORDER BY start_day
```
(NOTE: must filter `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` — excludes 'lead'/'lost' rows which are leads that never converted. Table has ALL leads, not just converted subscribers.)
Data through day98: start_day 49-62 churn 11.7%→32.3% (gradual rise, one cluster's worth of exposure, day69-72 event). start_day 63-68: **54.9%-61.7%** (got hit by BOTH day69-72 AND day92-95 clusters within their 30-day window — worse than a "typical" single-shock cohort will see going forward).

## ⭐ ACTIONS TAKEN DAY98 (decisive defensive pivot — cash preservation is now #1 priority)
1. **Ad spend CUT TO $0 (from $2,000/day = $14,000/week).** Evidence: conversion collapsed to ~5% uniformly across ALL sources (paid AND organic/network), meaning paid spend has ZERO conversion advantage over free leads right now. CAC had risen to ~$95-112/subscriber while LTV (given 55%+ churn) is only ~$18-30/subscriber net contribution — ads were purely value-destructive. Organic/network leads (~695-750/week) continue for free and give plenty of signal to monitor conversion-rate recovery. **Saves $14,000/week.**
2. **Dev spend reallocated: cut S2/S3/D_S10/D_S04 targeted dev to $0 (was $205+230+160+80=$675/day combined), kept S1 targeted at $550/day (unchanged) and global at $235/day (unchanged).** Rationale: those 4 small groups have only ~126 subscribers combined (S2:25,S3:50,D_S10:46,D_S04:5) vs S1's 6,403 (98% of business) — spending $80/day on D_S04 (5 subscribers!) is absurd leverage. Concentrate the (still-small, log-saturating) dev quality lever where it matters. **Saves $4,725/week.**
3. **Capacity tier downgraded Tier3→Tier2 (2.5M/day cap, $1,330/day → 800K/day cap, $530/day).** Usage now ~550K/day (was ~568K avg this week), 14-day peak was 731K (day93, when subscriber base was ~7,662 and rising ad spend was still active) — with subs now 6,533 and FALLING (per every forecast scenario), margin should only improve. Real but modest overload risk accepted given how critical cash preservation is. **Saves $5,600/week. MUST monitor next week's actual usage-vs-800K-cap closely — upgrade back immediately if utilization exceeds ~85-90% or any overload/outage occurs.**
4. **Ops HELD FLAT at $1,100/day** (did not cut further, did not increase). Reasoning: issue backlog shrinking fine (3,919→~3,359 per DB), resolution time stable ~3.5-4.3 days/issue over past 2 weeks regardless of small spend changes — no evidence of a resolution-speed crisis despite a notable cluster of 5 social posts (day98) complaining about slow/no support response (4-5 days, "vanished" tickets). These complaints are a REAL, longstanding pattern (recurring since ~day36) but are secondary to the quality-gap crisis, which dominates churn. Chose not to gamble more cash on an unproven lever this week; revisit if backlog stops shrinking.
5. **Pricing ($19/$99/$179), tiers (A=2/B=4/C=5), quotas, promotions (S1 $2 ongoing, S3 Plan-C $90, lead promos), ads_strength (S1 0.55): ALL HELD FLAT.** Deliberately did NOT test a price cut this week despite the temptation (lower price → lower required-quality-bar per the quality-price curve) — wanted to isolate the effect of the ad/capacity/dev cuts cleanly before adding another variable. **Reconsider a price-cut experiment next week or the week after** if conversion is still stuck ~5% (see To-Do).
6. **Total weekly cost reduction from these changes: ~$24,325/week** (14,000+4,725+5,600), against continued elevated churn. Net effect: should turn this week's -$24,599 burn into something much closer to breakeven or a small loss (~-$5K to +$5K) for the IMMEDIATE next week, though the multi-week reckoning wave (see above) will keep pressuring subscriber count/revenue down for the next 3-4 weeks regardless of cost cuts.
7. **Posted social media reply (agent_post_id=11, day98)** replying to post_id 193 (detailed complaint: "87% accuracy, beats stack by 12pts, BUT support ghosted after auto-reply, 5-day silence") — genuine, transparent tone acknowledging the issue + concrete offer (reply/DM ticket # for expedited escalation), consistent with the playbook that scored positively ~9+ times before.   - "First-eval" cohorts (start_day 69-75, first 30-day eval since signup):

  - "Repeat-eval" cohorts (start_day 39-45, SECOND 30-day eval): 8.3%-22.0%,
    weighted avg 14.8% -- MUCH lower than first-eval. Strong evidence for the
    "one-time reckoning" theory: tenure-loyalty bonus (grows with ln(1+months))
    helps existing customers pass subsequent evals even though brand-new leads
    (zero tenure) cannot pass at ANY price right now.

Model: track every active cohort (start_day, count), simulate forward,
apply first_eval_churn at their first 30-day mark >= day105, repeat_eval_churn

import json, random

with open('cohorts_day105.json') as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

CURRENT_DAY = 105
CASH_NOW = 128427.82

# cost structure (weekly), held flat
OPS = 1100*7

AVG_MONTHLY_PRICE = 17.81  # weighted avg effective price across active book

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # cohorts: list of [start_day, count, evals_done]

        if new_n > 0:
            cohorts.append([day, new_n, 0])

and churning customers who fail their eval don't generate that cycle's payment.
This version simulates billing/eval EXACTLY at each cohort's true 30-day mark:
survivors of the eval pay for their new cycle at that moment; between billing
marks, a cohort contributes zero NEW revenue that week (matches lumpy reality).
Also adds ad_revenue (smooth, daily, not billing-cycle-dependent) separately.
"""
import json

with open('cohorts_day105.json') as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

AVG_MONTHLY_PRICE = 17.81

- When a metric looks contradictory (e.g., dashboard "Open Issues: 1673" vs DB query "3005" using `status='open'`), don't assume a bug — trust the dashboard for absolute levels, use DB queries for trend/rate analysis (avg resolution days, new-vs-resolved pace) where the exact reconciliation matters less than the direction of travel.

"""
Forecast model v3 -- Week 15 (day105). Fixes revenue timing: billing happens
in a LUMPY fashion exactly at each cohort's 30-day marks (not smoothly spread
across all days as v1/v2 assumed). Empirical check: v2's smooth-rate assumption
predicted ~$26K/wk sub-revenue but actual was only $14.3K this week (46% lower) --
because only ~13% of the book bills in a given week (not the naive 23.3%=7/30),
and churning customers who fail their eval don't generate that cycle's payment.
This version simulates billing/eval EXACTLY at each cohort's true 30-day mark:
survivors of the eval pay for their new cycle at that moment; between billing
marks, a cohort contributes zero NEW revenue that week (matches lumpy reality).
Also adds ad_revenue (smooth, daily, not billing-cycle-dependent) separately.
"""
import json

with open('cohorts_day105.json') as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

CURRENT_DAY = 105
CASH_NOW = 128427.82
COMPUTE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY = 0.166
LEADS_PER_SUB_PER_WEEK = 841/6306.0
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
AD_REV_PER_SUB_PER_DAY = 0.0612
AVG_MONTHLY_PRICE = 17.81
USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY = 85.0

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10_000)]

def pick_capacity_tier(active_total):
    usage_est = active_total * USAGE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_est <= cap * 0.65:
            return cap, cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1]

def simulate(weeks, first_eval_churn, repeat_eval_churn, new_signups_per_week_fn):
    cohorts = []
    for row in cohorts_raw:
        sd = row['start_day']
        evals_done_initial = (CURRENT_DAY - sd) // 30
        cohorts.append([sd, row['active'], evals_done_initial])
    cash = CASH_NOW
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    trace = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks+1):
        new_n = new_signups_per_week_fn(wk)
        if new_n > 0:
            cohorts.append([day, new_n, 0])
        week_billing_revenue = 0.0
        for d in range(7):
            cur_day = day + d + 1
            for c in cohorts:
                start_day, count, evals_done = c
                if count <= 0:
                    continue
                next_eval_day = start_day + 30*(evals_done+1)
                if cur_day == next_eval_day:
                    rate = first_eval_churn if evals_done == 0 else repeat_eval_churn
                    survivors = count - count*rate
                    c[1] = survivors
                    c[2] = evals_done + 1
                    week_billing_revenue += survivors * AVG_MONTHLY_PRICE  # pay for new cycle
        day += 7
        active_total = sum(c[1] for c in cohorts)

        cap_units, cap_cost = pick_capacity_tier(active_total)
        ops_spend = max(300.0, 1100.0 * active_total/6079.0)
        if cash < 30_000:
            dev_spend = 0.0
        elif cash < 70_000:
            dev_spend = 235.0
        else:
            dev_spend = 785.0

        ad_revenue = active_total * AD_REV_PER_SUB_PER_DAY * 7
        leads = active_total * LEADS_PER_SUB_PER_WEEK
        lead_acq = leads * LEAD_ACQ_COST
        compute_cost = active_total * COMPUTE_PER_SUB_PER_DAY * 7
        total_cost = ops_spend*7 + dev_spend*7 + cap_cost*7 + compute_cost + lead_acq
        net = week_billing_revenue + ad_revenue - total_cost
        cash += net
        trace.append(dict(week=wk, day=day, active=active_total, cash=cash, net=net,
                           bill_rev=week_billing_revenue, ad_rev=ad_revenue, cost=total_cost))
    return trace

def zero_signups(wk):
    return 0

def bull_signups(wk):
    if wk <= 8:
        return 0
    return min(200, (wk-8)*12)

scenarios = {
    'bear': dict(first_eval_churn=0.65, repeat_eval_churn=0.28, signups=zero_signups),
    'base': dict(first_eval_churn=0.585, repeat_eval_churn=0.18, signups=zero_signups),
    'bull': dict(first_eval_churn=0.50, repeat_eval_churn=0.12, signups=bull_signups),
}

horizons_weeks = {'1wk':1, '4wk':4, '12wk':12, '26wk':26}
results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    trace = simulate(26, params['first_eval_churn'], params['repeat_eval_churn'], params['signups'])
    results[name] = trace
    print(f"--- {name} ---")
    for wk in range(1, 6):
        t = trace[wk-1]
        print(f"   wk{wk} day{t['day']}: active={t['active']:.0f} bill_rev=${t['bill_rev']:.0f} "
              f"ad_rev=${t['ad_rev']:.0f} cost=${t['cost']:.0f} net=${t['net']:.0f} cash=${t['cash']:,.0f}")
    for hname, hwk in horizons_weeks.items():
        t = trace[hwk-1]
        print(f"  {hname}: day{t['day']} active={t['active']:.0f} cash=${t['cash']:,.0f}")
    print()

weights = {'bear':0.35, 'base':0.40, 'bull':0.25}
print("=== BLENDED ===")
for hname, hwk in horizons_weeks.items():
    blended_cash = sum(weights[n]*results[n][hwk-1]['cash'] for n in weights)
    lo = min(results[n][hwk-1]['cash'] for n in weights)
    hi = max(results[n][hwk-1]['cash'] for n in weights)
    print(f"{hname}: point=${blended_cash:,.0f}  range=[{lo:,.0f}, {hi:,.0f}]")

- `get_group_insights(group_id)` shows `quality_floor_q_min` per group (e.g., S1=0.081, noisy ±65%) plus network/reputation influence weights — but this number is much LOWER than our actual delivered quality (~0.30), so it's likely NOT the binding constraint on new-lead conversion (some other, higher, time-varying "expected quality at price" bar — not directly queryable — is what's actually failing). Don't over-index on this field.
- `get_market_overview()` group names: S1=Price-Sensitive Individuals, S2=Quality-Focused Individuals, S3=Power Users (correcting a prior mis-assumption that S3 was quality-focused).

## To-Do / Check every week
1. **TOP PRIORITY: snapshot `{start_day: active}` (save as `cohorts_dayXXX.json`) and diff against LAST week's snapshot file** to get clean marginal per-cohort churn (first-eval remainder of 83-92 band this coming week/next; new repeat-eval bands each week). This is now the core forecasting input — keep doing it every week, it's working well (validated to exact payment-count precision).
2. Check whether S1 (or others) keep converting a small trickle at full-comp lead promo (~1%/wk expected, ~6/wk in absolute terms at current lead volume) — not enough to change strategy, just keep tracking.
3. Re-check `social_media_posts WHERE day > 112` for new competitor "quality boost" events before finalizing actions each week.
4. Monitor capacity utilization vs Tier2 (800K cap) — 70.8% peak this week, comfortable. Usage/sub trending down slightly (~77-80 vs 85 historically) as base shrinks — reconsider Tier1 downgrade only if peak usage falls under ~130K/day sustained (Tier1 cap=200K, want ~35% headroom).
5. Re-evaluate R&D/research_market only once cash is stable/growing and clearly above ~$250-300K — not there yet, and current trajectory (base case) doesn't clearly get there within 26 weeks either. May need proactive cost cuts later to ever afford it — reassess in a few weeks once more repeat-churn data confirms the stabilization holds.
6. Query `predictions` table each week for calibration tracking. 1wk horizon calibration is excellent so far — keep an eye on whether 4wk/12wk/26wk accuracy improves too as more of those resolve.
7. If cash drops below ~$80-100K, escalate: cut ops further, cut S1 dev too, consider deeper capacity downgrade (see forecast model's built-in thresholds for reference values).
8. Don't re-test ads_strength=0 or expanding S1's lead_promo cap above $19 unless genuinely new information emerges (both reasoned through this week, see crisis section — neither looks like a good trade right now).

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons)
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. `list_research_projects()` and `get_market_overview()`/`get_group_insights()` are free/read-only and safe anytime.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend` lives in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`.
- `docs/api/marketing.json`'s stated dev-spend coefficients (0.006/0.030) are WRONG — trust empirical calibration (0.0045/0.0225) confirmed by repeated week-over-week matches. But its `set_ads_strength` formula description (log-scaled, proportional revenue/penalty) checked out and was USEFUL — worth reading the docs closely for the mechanism even when specific numbers elsewhere have been wrong.
- **Flat/smooth-rate models are consistently wrong in this simulator: (1) churn is lumpy at 30-day cohort marks; (2) revenue realization is also lumpy, tied to the same 30-day marks.** Always build cohort-level, event-driven simulations for forecasting. This week validated the approach to EXACT payment-count precision (979 predicted = 979 actual) — high confidence in this method now.
- **For churn-rate estimation, prefer week-over-week snapshot diffs per cohort (`cohorts_dayXXX.json` vs previous week's file) over single-snapshot cumulative queries** — the latter conflates multiple eval cycles (e.g., a cohort that's had 2 evals shows cumulative churn from BOTH, not the rate of either one alone) and can mislead if evals happened at different times (some pre-shock, some post-shock).
- A single blended/mixed-window data point (pre- and post-shock days averaged) can mask a much more extreme true current-state rate — always isolate cleanly by the relevant dimension (time, cohort, eval-number) rather than averaging across a heterogeneous window.
- Competitor event clusters vary hugely in magnitude (day69-72 ~0.09-0.10/event, day92-95 ~0.13-0.17/event, day103-106 ~0.03-0.035/event) and are the single biggest source of forecast error — unpredictable timing/magnitude. Mitigants: large cash buffer, continuous (cheap) dev investment, fast reaction via social-media monitoring.
- Before assuming a "free lunch" experiment (e.g., cutting ads_strength) is worth doing, read the exact formula in the docs first — sometimes a lever that looks like "pure downside reduction" is actually a proportional trade-off with no free region (ads_strength case this week). Reasoning from the formula saved a wasted, irreversible-feeling experiment.
- When cash preservation is critical, highest-leverage cuts in order of $-impact-per-strategic-cost: (1) ad spend once conversion craters (near-zero opportunity cost), (2) capacity right-sizing to actual usage, (3) targeted dev spend on tiny/marginal groups (redirect to dominant group), (4) ops spend (higher opportunity cost, cut last — currently earning its keep: 1.63-day avg issue resolution, shrinking backlog, no outages).
- All `by_group`/`by_channel`/`by_customer` dicts for `set_targeted_*`/`set_promotion`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength` are FULL-REPLACEMENT — pass the complete desired allocation every time, omitting a key zeros it out. (If making NO changes, simply don't call the function at all — settings persist across weeks automatically.)
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can misbehave. Prefer writing a script file and running `./novamind-operation python script.py` for anything non-trivial.
- When a metric looks contradictory (e.g., dashboard "Open Issues: 1,452" vs DB query "2,922" using `status='open'`), don't assume a bug — trust the dashboard for absolute levels, use DB queries for trend/rate analysis (avg resolution days, new-vs-resolved pace) where the exact reconciliation matters less than the direction of travel.
- `subscriptions` table has no `price` column — use `effective_price`. `customers` table has no `segment` column — use `customer_type` (values include "Enterprise").

import novamind_api as nm

# Get all resolved predictions (target day <= current day)
current_day = nm.vars.current_day
r = nm.query(f"SELECT submit_day, horizon_days, predicted_value, predicted_lower, predicted_upper FROM predictions WHERE submit_day + horizon_days <= {current_day} ORDER BY submit_day, horizon_days")

preds = r['rows']

# Get cumulative cash at each needed target day
target_days = sorted(set(p['submit_day'] + p['horizon_days'] for p in preds))
cash_by_day = {}
for td in target_days:
    rr = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger WHERE day <= {td}")
    cash_by_day[td] = rr['rows'][0]['cash']

print(f"{'submit':>7} {'horizon':>8} {'target':>7} {'pred':>10} {'lower':>10} {'upper':>10} {'actual':>10} {'err%':>7} {'in_CI':>6}")
for p in preds:
    target = p['submit_day'] + p['horizon_days']
    actual = cash_by_day[target]
    err_pct = (actual - p['predicted_value']) / p['predicted_value'] * 100 if p['predicted_value'] else float('nan')
    in_ci = p['predicted_lower'] <= actual <= p['predicted_upper']
    print(f"{p['submit_day']:>7} {p['horizon_days']:>8} {target:>7} {p['predicted_value']:>10.0f} {p['predicted_lower']:>10.0f} {p['predicted_upper']:>10.0f} {actual:>10.0f} {err_pct:>6.1f}% {str(in_ci):>6}")
