# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory (updated day210)

## ⚰️ VERDICT day210: PRICING EXPERIMENT FAILED — LEVER CONFIRMED DEAD. Game is now in permanent COAST / cost-floor-minimization phase.
**The day203 aggressive price cut (A:$5, B:$20) was the last real lever tried.** Result via exact cohort comparison (`compare_cohorts_210.py`): of the 311 customers whose cohort hit its 30-day eval boundary days204-210 (billed/evaluated UNDER the new $5/$20 price), **310 churned (99.68%), only 1 survived** (an S1 customer on Plan B @ $20). This is statistically indistinguishable from the 100% churn observed the prior week at the OLD $19/$99 price. **Conclusion: price is not, and was never, the binding constraint — the quality-vs-expectation gap (driven by cumulative competitor drift + our inability to afford dev/R&D at scale) is fundamentally insurmountable at our current cash level.** My q_min-margin theory from day203 was WRONG (or at least insufficient) — a huge nominal margin over the $0-price quality floor did not translate into rescued retention. Do not attempt further pricing experiments — there is no evidence base left to justify one.

**New leads also confirm this: 42 new leads arrived day204-210, ZERO converted to subscribers (even at the $5 price).** New-customer conversion is 0% regardless of price — same root cause (quality gap), not a pricing/promotion problem.

### Why we can't fix the root cause
- R&D Tier 1 costs $166,667 — cash is $89,181 and **monotonically decreasing** under the coast strategy (no revenue lever left), so R&D will NEVER become affordable again. Permanently off the table.
- Dev spend quality formula is log-saturating (0.0045×ln(1+spend/5000) global, 5x for targeted) — even $50K/day forever only buys ~+0.01 quality. Utterly insufficient against competitor drift, and unaffordable at our scale anyway.
- Capacity tier 0 ($85/day) is the **absolute floor** — reconfirmed via `get_cost_info()` again day210. No tier below 0, no "off" state. This fixed fee is unavoidable for the rest of the game (294 days remaining as of day210 → ~$25K total floor cost through day504).

## 📊 CURRENT STATE day210
- Cash: $89,180.60 (exact, `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`)
- Active individual subs: 173 (S1-A:153, D_S10-A:11, S2-A:7, S1-B:1, S2-B:1). Enterprise: 0 (still, 100+ days dead).
- **Remaining 173 will almost entirely churn within the next 2-3 weeks** per exact eval schedule (`upcoming_evals_210.py`): 137 due days211-217, 35 due days218-222, 1 lone straggler (the day203 survivor, S1/Plan-B) due day234. At ~99.7% churn rate, expect active count → ~0 by day~225, maybe 1 residual until day234.
- **IMPORTANT NEW FINDING: remaining active (pre-churn) subscribers are net CASH-NEGATIVE on a daily basis**, not positive! Calibrated day210: compute cost ≈ $0.199/sub/day vs ad_revenue ≈ $0.082/sub/day vs lead_acq ≈$0.012/sub/day → net ≈ **-$0.128/sub/day burn** (compute cost exceeds ad revenue). This is because virtually nobody renews (pays subscription fee) anymore — the old "customers are net positive because of ad_revenue vs compute" logic ONLY holds if they pay their subscription fee at renewal, which ~100% no longer do. Correction to earlier (day203) memory note — retract "more retained customers = more cash" claim; it's now mildly the reverse (more residual subs = slightly MORE burn until they finish churning out), though the $ magnitude is small (<$25/day at current scale).
- No lever changes needed this week — all settings already at coast-optimal: ops=$0, dev=$0, capacity=Tier0, ad_spend=$0 (all channels/groups), ads_strength=1.0 global (free, keep — still generates ad_revenue). Prices left at $5/$20/$179 (unchanged — no evidence changing them helps or hurts at this point; not worth the risk of perturbing the ~1 surviving customer who passed at $20).
- Posted social media reply #27 day210 (accountability tone, reply to post_id=540, a fresh 5+day-support-ticket complaint). Same pattern as posts 20-27, still free/no downside. Note: `effect_by_group` on these posts is consistently POSITIVE for S1/S3/E3 but NEGATIVE (-0.6 to -0.7) for E1/E2/D_E-groups (large enterprises read "CEO personally intervenes" as evidence of systemic dysfunction, want SLAs not heroics) — irrelevant since Enterprise is dead and we're not pursuing it.
- Competitor "quality boost" mentions day206-209: small/normal magnitude (0.0246-0.0339, several mentions) — NOT another acceleration cluster like day190-195. No action needed, just noting for the record. (Day195 had one big 0.1697 mention, already reflected in past drift.)

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL — pure cost-floor decay simulation (`forecast_wk30.py`)
Exact cohort-scheduled churn-decay model: 173 active decaying via known eval-day schedule at ~99.68% churn rate (empirically observed), net burn = $85/day fixed capacity + active_count × $0.1284/day (net compute-minus-ad-revenue-minus-leadacq burn). Sensitivity-tested churn rate 90%-100%: **final cash is barely sensitive to the exact churn rate** (26wk range only $73,204-$73,597 across the whole 90%-100% churn spectrum) because (a) surviving subs are net-negative anyway, not a meaningful revenue source, and (b) the dominant term by far is the unavoidable $85/day×remaining-days fixed cost.
Base case (churn=99.68%) results from day210 cash $89,180.60:
| Horizon | Day | Cash | Active remaining |
|---|---|---|---|
| +7d | 217 | $88,483 | ~36 |
| +28d | 238 | $86,685 | ~0.6 |
| +84d | 294 | $81,921 | ~0.6 |
| +182d | 392 | $73,584 | ~0.6 |

**Submitted (day210):** 1wk=$88,480[$88,150,$88,750]; 4wk=$86,680[$86,000,$87,300]; 12wk=$81,900[$80,200,$83,400]; 26wk=$73,550[$70,500,$76,500]. Tight-ish CIs reflecting the now very low-variance, almost purely mechanical fixed-cost regime — widened somewhat at longer horizons for compounding model/calibration uncertainty and small tail risk (e.g. unexpected costs, or a strategy change if something changes).

**Last week's forecast (day203) accuracy check:** predicted 1wk=$89,450[$88,800,$90,400], actual day210=$89,181 — 0.3% error, within CI. Good, cohort-exact model keeps validating.

## 📋 GO-FORWARD PLAN (simplified — nothing left to optimize but cost floor)
1. **No further pricing/spend experiments planned.** All discretionary levers (ads, promotions, dev, ops, R&D, enterprise) have been tested and confirmed dead or unaffordable across 30 weeks of play. The only remaining "decision" is to minimize burn, which is already at the floor.
2. **Weekly routine going forward should be LIGHTWEIGHT:**
   - Confirm cash (`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`) and active subscriber count.
   - Quick-check social posts for a complaint to reply to (free, habitual, keep doing it — takes 2 min).
   - Re-run cohort snapshot + comparison ONE more time around day217/224 to confirm population fully bottoms out near 0 as predicted — after that, cohort tracking becomes unnecessary (nobody left to track) and can stop.
   - Re-verify config hasn't drifted (`config_history` latest row) — cheap sanity check, should always show ops=0,dev=0,capacity_tier=0,ad_spend=0.
   - Submit forecast using the simple fixed-cost model: cash(t) ≈ cash_now − $85×days_elapsed (once population ~0), or use `forecast_wk30.py`-style script adjusted for updated cash/day if any small residual population remains.
   - Advance. No need for elaborate weekly investigation anymore — the game is now a solved, static optimization (minimize burn, which we're already doing).
3. **One thing to keep an eye on (low probability but check occasionally, e.g. every 4-8 weeks):** is there truly no way to reduce capacity below Tier 0 / $85/day? Re-verified multiple times now (day196, day203, day210) — consistently no. Don't keep re-checking every single week, maybe once a month for sanity.
4. **If, against expectation, active subscriber count stops declining / stabilizes at some meaningfully positive number (i.e. my churn-to-zero prediction is wrong), STOP and re-investigate** — that would be a surprising finding worth a fresh full analysis (would mean tenure-loyalty bonus or some other factor is stabilizing a subpopulation long-term, which could change the optimal strategy, e.g. reconsider targeted dev spend on that surviving subgroup).

## Game basics (confirmed from live API — stable facts, keep)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day210, cash $89,180.60. Active individual subs=173 (was 483 day203, 1087 day196, 1546 day189 — collapse continuing, now nearly complete).**
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- **`ledger` columns are `day, category, amount, note` (NOT `type`).** Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment (only appears on days someone actually renews — rare now).
- **Churn/billing mechanic (re-confirmed 11th+ time): evaluated EXACTLY when tenure crosses a multiple of 30 (`(day - start_day) % 30 == 0`). Survivors rebilled at CURRENT price/promo; churners pay nothing and leave. Between boundaries, churn is exactly 0%.** Always model with exact cohort day arithmetic (`snapshot_cohorts.py` + `upcoming_evals_XXX.py` + `compare_cohorts_XXX.py` — all still in working dir, reusable pattern).
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/$85/day (CURRENT, FLOOR — no lower tier or "off" state exists), T1=200K/$215, T2=800K/$530, T3=2.5M/$1330, T4=8M/$4000, T5=25M/$10000, T6=80M/$28000, T7=300M/$75000. Model tier compute $/unit: tier1=0.0003, tier2=0.002(Plan A), tier3=0.006, tier4=0.012(Plan B), tier5=0.03(Plan C). Capacity cost is a pure fixed daily fee regardless of usage/subscriber count (confirmed: charged exactly $85.00 every single day day204-210 despite population dropping 483→173).
- Calibrated day210 (from exact day-by-day ledger, `daily_usage`, `ads_revenue` tables at stable post-cancellation population of 173): **compute ≈ $0.1987/sub/day, ad_revenue ≈ $0.0823/sub/day, lead_acq ≈ ~$0.012/sub/day** (leads scale ∝ active count, ~0.024 leads/day/sub × $0.5/lead). Net variable burn ≈ **-$0.1284/sub/day** (subscribers are now a small net cash DRAG, not a source of profit, since renewal-payment is ~never collected anymore).
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads ever, 100+ days confirmed dead. Just note "still 0" going forward, no deep-dive needed.
- `post_social_media`: keep weekly cadence (works fine, no fatigue after 7 uses). 27 posts total now (agent_post_id 20-27 all "accountability" replies to support complaints).
- `subscriptions.status` valid values: `'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost'`. `customers.customer_type`: `'small'`/`'large'`. Use `effective_price` not `price`. Use `c.group_id` (join customers), NOT `subscriptions.group_id` (doesn't exist — subscriptions has customer_id/plan/listed_price/promotion/effective_price/start_day/end_day/status/billing_day_mod30/seat_count/pending_plan/pending_price/contract_months/contract_end_day).
- `config_history` table (daily snapshot: price_A/B/C, tier_A/B/C, spend_advertising/operations/development, capacity_tier, ad_spend_<channel>, quota_A/B/C) — use `ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` for quick "what's set now" checks (much better than dumping `config_overrides`, which can return a HUGE historical by_customer dict blob from old promotions — avoid unfiltered `SELECT *` on config_overrides, it can blow past output limits).
- R&D: unaffordable ($166,667 Tier1 vs cash $89,180) and will only get LESS affordable as cash decays under the coast strategy. Permanently shelved.

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons)
- **NEW (day210): a large nominal margin between delivered quality and quality_floor_q_min (at price=$0) does NOT guarantee a price cut will rescue retention — verified via a real experiment (99.68% churn even at $5, same as 100% at $19). Trust live experiments over theoretical margin calculations; info_level=1 (±65%) noise on group insights can be badly wrong even directionally.**
- **NEW (day210): don't assume "more retained subscribers = more cash" — check the actual per-sub daily P&L (compute cost vs ad_revenue vs lead_acq) directly from the ledger. Once renewal/conversion rates collapse to ~0%, residual subscribers can become net cash-NEGATIVE (compute cost > ad revenue) since the subscription-payment revenue that used to offset compute cost is no longer being collected.**
- **NEW (day210): when a strategic conclusion is "coast / do nothing new," the weekly routine can and should be simplified — don't keep re-running expensive deep-dives (cohort tracking, enterprise checks, R&D affordability checks) every single week once the answer has stabilized. Match effort to the decision-relevance of the check.**
- **NEW (day210): avoid unfiltered `SELECT * FROM config_overrides` — old promotion calls can have massive by_customer dicts (hundreds of entries) that blow through output limits. Use `config_history ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` for current settings, or add specific WHERE/LIMIT clauses.**
- Competitor quality-boost shocks can cluster/accelerate sharply (10x normal magnitude) then stop just as suddenly — always scan the FULL week of social posts, don't assume a cluster means a new permanent trend.
- Don't assume a lever is "fully exploited" just because it's non-zero — always check the actual live config (`config_history` for prices/tiers/quotas/spend) rather than trusting a stale memory summary.
- `effective_price`/`promotion` fields only update AT the customer's next billing event, not immediately when you change global settings.
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Free/read-only: `list_research_projects()`, `get_market_overview()`, `get_group_insights()`, all table queries via `nm.query()`.
- Social-media view counts are noisy — don't over-fit narratives to a couple of data points.
- For revenue/cash forecasting, always use EXACT day-by-day cohort billing simulation, never amortized/smoothed weekly approximation — this approach has been consistently accurate (~0.3-0.6% weekly forecast error, many weeks running).
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` live in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`/`post_social_media` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion`/`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`, requires BOTH operations and development every call.
- `social_media_posts` table has NO author_type/sentiment columns. Our own posts + performance metrics are in `agent_social_media_posts`.
- python-c with complex nested quotes/heredocs can misbehave — prefer writing a script file and running `./novamind-operation python script.py`.
- CLI daily-script management is via the separate `novamind` binary (register-daily-script/list-daily-scripts/remove-daily-script), NOT `novamind-operation`. 0 scripts currently registered.

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory (updated day217)

## ⚰️ STATUS: PERMANENT COAST / COST-FLOOR-MINIMIZATION PHASE (confirmed again day217, no change)
All discretionary levers (pricing, ads, promotions, dev, ops, R&D, enterprise) tested and confirmed dead/unaffordable across 31 weeks. Nothing left to optimize but the fixed cost floor, which is already at minimum (Tier 0 capacity, $0 ops/dev/ads). **Do not re-litigate this — see day189-210 memory history (in git/old notes) for the full evidence trail if ever in doubt.**

## 📊 CURRENT STATE day217
- Cash: $88,501.83 (exact, `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`). **Forecast accuracy check: day210 predicted 1wk=$88,480[$88,150,$88,750] for day217 → actual $88,502 = 0.02% error, comfortably inside CI. Model continues to validate extremely well.**
- Active individual subs: 36 (S1-A:27, S2-A:4, D_S10-A:3, S1-B:1, S2-B:1). Enterprise: 0 (confirmed again, 0 rows ever in `enterprise_turns` — permanently dead, no need to keep re-querying this every week, check ~monthly at most).
- Cancellations this week: 137 (exactly matched prediction from day210 memory). New leads: 17 (all still converting to 0 new subscribers — 0% conversion regime continues, unchanged since day203 price cut).
- **Exact eval schedule for remaining 36 (queried directly from `subscriptions.start_day` mod-30 arithmetic):** 17 evaluated day218, 9 day219, 4 day220, 2 day221, 3 day222 (=35 total this coming week), then a lone straggler **cust=12108 (S1, Plan B, $20/seat) due day234** — this is the SAME customer that survived the day203 price-cut cohort test (memory day210). At 99.68% empirical churn rate (now confirmed across 2 independent large cohorts: 311 customers days204-210, and prior 100% cohort before that), expect ~0-1 survivors from the 35 evaluated this week → population converging to ~0-1 by day222-224, then to ~0 by day234 (when 12108 gets its next eval) unless it beats the odds again.
- **No config changes made or needed.** ops=$0, dev=$0, capacity=Tier0, ad_spend=$0 all channels, prices A=$5/B=$20/C=$179 unchanged. `config_history` confirms no drift since day203.
- Posted social reply #28 day217 (accountability tone, reply to post_id=565, fresh "4 days no support response" S1 complaint). Zero cost, habitual, keep doing weekly — historically net-positive effect_by_group for S1/S2/S3 (our remaining population), even though negative for enterprise groups (irrelevant, enterprise is dead). No fatigue observed after 28 posts.
- Social feed: routine competitor "quality boost" mentions, small/normal magnitude (~0.0088-0.0099), no acceleration cluster. No action needed.

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL — now fully dominated by fixed $85/day capacity cost (`forecast_wk31.py`)
With population at 36 and converging to ~0-1 within 1-2 weeks, the variable per-subscriber burn (compute − ad_revenue − lead_acq, calibrated day217: compute_rate=$0.2576/sub/day, adrev_rate=$0.0806/sub/day) is now a rounding error next to the $85/day fixed capacity fee. **Going forward, cash(t) ≈ cash_now − $85 × (t − day_now), plus a small (<$50 total) transitional tail while the last few customers churn out over the next 1-2 weeks.** This closely matches the OLD (population=173) decay model's trajectory once you shift by the elapsed $85/day — good cross-validation between the two independently-built models.

Day217 baseline, results from `forecast_wk31.py` (exact schedule + 99.68% churn + calibrated rates):
| Horizon | Day | Cash (point) | Expected pop |
|---|---|---|---|
| +7d | 224 | $87,898 | ~1.1 |
| +28d | 245 | $86,110 | ~0.1 |
| +84d | 301 | $81,349 | ~0.1 |
| +182d | 399 | $73,017 | ~0.1 |

**Submitted (day217):** 1wk=$87,900[$87,700,$88,100]; 4wk=$86,100[$85,700,$86,500]; 12wk=$81,350[$80,500,$82,200]; 26wk=$73,000[$71,000,$75,000]. Tight CIs justified by the now near-fully-mechanical fixed-cost regime and strong track record of <0.5% weekly error; widened modestly at longer horizons for compounding/calibration uncertainty.

**Extrapolating to day504 (game end):** ~287 days remaining from day217 × $85/day ≈ $24,395 total future fixed cost (plus negligible variable tail) → expect final cash to land somewhere around **$64,000-$65,000** if nothing changes. This is now a highly predictable, low-variance number baked in almost entirely by the capacity floor fee. (Not a new lever to chase — just noting the expected end state.)

## 📋 GO-FORWARD PLAN (lightweight — confirmed working, keep doing this)
1. **Weekly routine (should take <10 min):**
   - Check dashboard cash + active subs (already shown automatically).
   - Quick social-post scan for a fresh complaint → reply (free, habitual, 2 min, positive EV).
   - Confirm config hasn't drifted (`config_history ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` — should always show day203 settings frozen: ops=0,dev=0,tier=0,ad_spend=0,prices 5/20/179).
   - Update cash/population numbers in this file, re-run `forecast_wk31.py`-style script (just bump `day`/`cash_now`/population inputs) for the 4 forecast horizons.
   - Submit forecast + rationale, advance.
2. **Once population hits ~0 (expected by day~222-234), cohort-tracking scripts become unnecessary** — at that point just use pure `cash(t) = cash_now - 85*(t-day_now)` with a tiny CI, and stop querying `subscriptions`/eval schedules entirely (nothing left to track). Check back only if population count in dashboard surprises us (see #4 below).
3. **Capacity-floor-existence check**: re-verified multiple times (day196/203/210), consistently no tier below 0. Don't re-check again until ~day260+ (quarterly cadence is plenty).
4. **STOP AND RE-INVESTIGATE IF:** active subscriber count stops declining / stabilizes at a meaningfully positive number (i.e., churn-to-zero prediction wrong), OR cash trajectory deviates from the fixed-cost model by more than ~2-3% in a week (would indicate a mechanic we don't understand, e.g. a hidden floor-cost change, or the 12108-style survivor turning out to represent a bigger stable sub-population than expected). Otherwise, no need for deep dives — this is now a solved, static optimization.

## Game basics (confirmed from live API — stable facts, keep)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day217, cash $88,501.83. Active individual subs=36 (was 173 day210, 483 day203 — collapse essentially complete, final tail now playing out).**
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- `ledger` columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment (rare now).
- **Churn/billing mechanic (re-confirmed many times): evaluated EXACTLY when tenure crosses a multiple of 30 (`(day - start_day) % 30 == 0`). Survivors rebilled at CURRENT price/promo; churners pay nothing and leave. Between boundaries, churn is exactly 0%.** Query `subscriptions.start_day` + current day to get exact future eval days per customer — this has been a reliable, reusable pattern all game (see `week31_evals.py`).
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/$85/day (FLOOR — confirmed no lower tier exists, checked 3+ times), T1=200K/$215, up to T7=300M/$75000. Capacity fee is a pure fixed daily charge regardless of usage/subscriber count.
- Compute $/unit by model tier: tier1=0.0003, tier2=0.002(Plan A), tier3=0.006, tier4=0.012(Plan B), tier5=0.03(Plan C).
- Calibrated day217 (population=36, near-floor regime): compute≈$0.2576/sub/day, ad_revenue≈$0.0806/sub/day, lead_acq≈$0.5/lead (~1-2/day at this population). Net variable burn per sub ≈ -$0.18/day, i.e. still a small net drag, but now totally immaterial in dollar terms given population is ~1-36.
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads EVER (confirmed again day217 via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enterprise_turns` = 0). Permanently dead — stop checking weekly, monthly is plenty.
- `post_social_media`: 1/week cadence works fine, no fatigue after 28 uses. `effect_by_group` consistently positive (+0.3 to +0.65) for S1/S2/S3/D_S* on "accountability" replies to support complaints, negative for E1/E2/E3/D_E* (irrelevant now, enterprise dead).
- `subscriptions.status`: `'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost'`. `customers.customer_type`: `'small'`/`'large'`. Use `effective_price` not `price`. Join `c.group_id` from customers (subscriptions has no group_id column).
- `config_history`: daily snapshot table, `ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` for current settings — much cheaper/safer than dumping `config_overrides` (avoid unfiltered `SELECT *` there, can return huge historical by_customer blobs).
- R&D: permanently unaffordable (Tier1 $166,667 vs cash <$90K and shrinking). Shelved for good.

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons — see git history/old notes for the full day189-210 experiment log if ever needed)
- A large nominal quality-vs-price margin does NOT guarantee a price cut rescues retention — verified via real experiment (99.68% churn even at aggressive $5 price cut, same as prior ~100% at $19). Trust live experiments over theoretical margin calcs; low info_level group insights (±65% noise) can be badly wrong directionally.
- Once renewal/conversion rates collapse to ~0%, residual subscribers can become net cash-NEGATIVE (compute cost > ad revenue), since subscription-payment revenue is no longer collected at renewal. Don't assume "more retained customers = more cash" — check actual per-sub P&L from the ledger directly.
- When a strategic conclusion is "coast / do nothing new," simplify the weekly routine to match — don't keep re-running expensive deep-dives every week once the answer has stabilized. This week's routine (cash check, social reply, config check, forecast) took a fraction of the time of the old cohort-comparison-heavy routine and captured everything decision-relevant.
- Avoid unfiltered `SELECT * FROM config_overrides` — old promotion calls can have massive by_customer dicts. Use `config_history ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` instead.
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Free/read-only: `list_research_projects()`, `get_market_overview()`, `get_group_insights()`, all table queries via `nm.query()`.
- For cash forecasting, always use EXACT day-by-day cohort billing simulation (known eval-day schedule + calibrated per-sub rates), never smoothed weekly approximation — this has been consistently accurate (<0.5% weekly error, many weeks running, including this week: 0.02% error).
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` live in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`/`post_social_media` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion`/`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`, requires BOTH operations and development every call.
- CLI daily-script management is via the separate `novamind` binary (register-daily-script/list-daily-scripts/remove-daily-script), NOT `novamind-operation`. 0 scripts currently registered.

# NovaMind CEO — Strategy Memory (updated day224)

## ⚰️ STATUS: PERMANENT COAST / COST-FLOOR-MINIMIZATION PHASE (confirmed again day224, no change)
All discretionary levers (pricing, ads, promotions, dev, ops, R&D, enterprise) tested and confirmed dead/unaffordable across 32 weeks. Nothing left to optimize — fixed cost floor (Tier 0 capacity, $85/day) now dominates everything. **Do not re-litigate — see day189-217 memory history (git) for full evidence trail.**

## 📊 CURRENT STATE day224
- Cash: $87,897.79 (`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`). **Forecast check: day217 predicted 1wk=$87,900[$87,700,$88,100] for day224 → actual $87,898 = 0.002% error. Model keeps validating essentially perfectly.**
- Active individual subs: **1** (customer 12108, S1, Plan B, $20/seat, start_day=54). This is the SAME survivor flagged since day203/210/217. Enterprise: 0 (0 rows ever in `enterprise_turns`, permanently dead — checked again day224, next check ~day260+).
- Cancellations this week: 35 (population went 36→1, matches prediction). New leads: 0, new subs: 0.
- **cust=12108 next billing eval: day234** (start_day=54; eval whenever (day-54)%30==0 → 54,84,...,204,234,264...). At ~99.68% empirical churn rate, expect churn at day234 with ~99.68% probability → population likely 0 from day234 onward. Small (~0.3%) chance it survives again like it has twice before.
- **No config changes made or needed.** ops=$0, dev=$0, capacity=Tier0, ad_spend=$0 all channels, prices A=$5/B=$20/C=$179 unchanged since day203 (`config_history` confirms).
- Posted social reply #29 day224 (accountability tone, reply to post_id=590, fresh S1-type complaint re: inconsistent quality/onboarding). Zero cost, habitual, positive EV, no fatigue after 29 uses.
- Social feed: mostly macro/PMI commentary + one genuine customer complaint (replied to). No competitor acceleration signal.

## 🔬 LEDGER CALIBRATION UPDATE (day217-224 daily breakdown, population declining 36→1 through the week)
Queried exact daily ledger by category — confirms capacity fee **charged flat $85.00/day regardless of population** (even at population=1, day223/224 both show exactly -$85.00). Compute cost decayed from -$9.27/day (day217, pop~30s) down to **-$0.036 to -$0.072/day** (day223/224, pop=1) — now near-zero. Ad_revenue similarly decayed and **stabilized at +$0.1275/day** (constant day223=day224). Net variable at population=1 is now **~+$0.05-0.09/day (slightly net POSITIVE — ad_revenue > compute)**, not negative as previously modeled at higher populations. This is immaterial in dollar terms (~$0.06/day × ~280 remaining days ≈ $17 total) — not worth any action, but corrects the sign of the old "-0.18/day drag" assumption from higher-population days. **New steady-state daily burn ≈ -$84.93/day, essentially indistinguishable from flat -$85/day.**

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL (script logic, reusable each week)
```
cash(t) = cash_now - 85*(t-day_now) + 0.06*min(t-day_now, days_to_next_eval)
```
The tiny variable correction only matters through cust=12108's next eval (day234); after that, treat as pure flat -$85/day (population will be ~0, or on the ~0.3% chance it survives, contributes another negligible +$0.06/day — don't bother modeling further, correction caps at ~$0.60 total forever, i.e. round-off dust).

Day224 baseline forecasts submitted:
| Horizon | Day | Cash (point) | CI width rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| +7d | 231 | $87,303 | ±0.46%, before day234 eval, pure deterministic |
| +28d | 252 | $85,518 | ±1.0%, spans the one eval event (tiny prob mass) |
| +84d | 308 | $80,758 | ±2.85%, longer horizon, small model-risk buffer |
| +182d | 406 | $72,428 | ±6.1%, widest — unknown-unknowns over 6 months |

**Extrapolating to day504 (game end):** ~280 days remaining × $85/day ≈ $23,800 total future fixed cost → expect final cash to land around **$64,000-$65,000** if nothing changes (consistent with prior week's projection — model is stable/self-consistent).

## 📋 GO-FORWARD PLAN (lightweight — keep doing this)
1. **Weekly routine (~10 min):**
   - Check dashboard cash + active subs (auto-shown).
   - Quick social-post scan for a fresh complaint → reply (free, habitual, 2 min, positive EV). Use `SELECT post_id, day, content FROM social_media_posts ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 8` (no `author_group` column — content-only + post_id/day).
   - Confirm config hasn't drifted (`config_history ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` — should show day203 settings frozen).
   - Recompute forecast via the formula above (just bump `cash_now`/`day_now`, and re-check cust=12108's status — once it churns, drop the +0.06/day correction entirely and go pure flat -$85/day).
   - Submit forecast + rationale, advance.
2. **Once population hits 0 (expected ~day234, maybe later if 12108 beats the odds a 3rd time):** switch to pure `cash(t) = cash_now - 85*(t-day_now)`, stop querying `subscriptions`/eval schedules — nothing left to track. Just confirm dashboard still shows 0 subs each week (5 second check).
3. **Capacity-floor-existence check**: re-verified many times (day196/203/210/217). Don't re-check until ~day260+.
4. **STOP AND RE-INVESTIGATE IF:** active subscriber count stops declining / stabilizes positive (churn-to-zero prediction wrong), OR cash trajectory deviates from flat -$85/day model by >2-3% in a week (would indicate a mechanic we don't understand). Otherwise no deep dives needed — solved, static optimization.

## Game basics (confirmed from live API — stable facts, keep)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day224, cash $87,897.79. Active individual subs=1 (was 36 day217, 173 day210, 483 day203 — collapse complete, final straggler now the whole story).**
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- `ledger` columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment (rare now).
- **Churn/billing mechanic (re-confirmed many times): evaluated EXACTLY when tenure crosses a multiple of 30 (`(day - start_day) % 30 == 0`). Survivors rebilled at CURRENT price/promo; churners pay nothing and leave. Between boundaries, churn is exactly 0%.**
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/$85/day (FLOOR — confirmed no lower tier exists, checked 4+ times), T1=200K/$215, up to T7=300M/$75000. Capacity fee is a pure fixed daily charge **regardless of usage/subscriber count, confirmed even at population=1**.
- Compute $/unit by model tier: tier1=0.0003, tier2=0.002(Plan A), tier3=0.006, tier4=0.012(Plan B), tier5=0.03(Plan C).
- Calibrated day224 (population=1, near-zero regime): compute≈$0.05/day, ad_revenue≈$0.1275/day (both now essentially flat/stable, tiny). Net variable is slightly POSITIVE (~+0.06/day) at this population — correction from earlier "-0.18/day" estimate which applied at higher populations (30s-100s).
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads EVER (confirmed again day224). Permanently dead — check ~monthly.
- `post_social_media`: 1/week cadence works fine, no fatigue after 29 uses. `effect_by_group` consistently positive for S1/S2/S3/D_S* on "accountability" replies to support complaints.
- `subscriptions.status` values: `'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost'` (NOT `'active'` — querying `status='active'` returns 0 rows silently-ish with a warning; always use `'subscribed'`).
- `customers.customer_type`: `'small'`/`'large'`. Use `effective_price` not `price`. Join `c.group_id` from customers (subscriptions has no group_id column).
- `social_media_posts` table columns are ONLY `post_id, day, content` — no `author_group`/`sentiment` column accessible via query (sentiment must be inferred from text, per game docs).
- `config_history`: daily snapshot table, `ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` for current settings — cheaper/safer than dumping `config_overrides` (avoid unfiltered `SELECT *` there).
- R&D: permanently unaffordable (Tier1 $166,667 vs cash <$90K and shrinking). Shelved for good.

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons)
- A large nominal quality-vs-price margin does NOT guarantee a price cut rescues retention — verified via real experiment (99.68% churn even at aggressive $5 price cut). Trust live experiments over theoretical margin calcs.
- Once renewal/conversion rates collapse to ~0%, residual subscribers can become net cash-negative OR slightly positive depending on population size (compute cost vs ad revenue don't scale identically) — always check actual per-sub P&L from the ledger directly rather than assuming a fixed sign for the "variable drag."
- When a strategic conclusion is "coast / do nothing new," simplify the weekly routine to match — don't keep re-running expensive deep-dives every week once the answer has stabilized.
- Avoid unfiltered `SELECT * FROM config_overrides` — old promotion calls can have massive by_customer dicts. Use `config_history ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 1` instead.
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Free/read-only: `list_research_projects()`, `get_market_overview()`, `get_group_insights()`, all table queries via `nm.query()`.
- For cash forecasting, always use EXACT day-by-day ledger-calibrated rates (query recent daily ledger by category), never smoothed multi-week-old averages — rates change materially as population shrinks (e.g. compute/ad_revenue both decayed ~100x from day217 to day224). This has been consistently accurate (<0.5% weekly error every week for over a month).
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` live in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`/`post_social_media` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion`/`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`, requires BOTH operations and development every call.
- CLI daily-script management is via the separate `novamind` binary (register-daily-script/list-daily-scripts/remove-daily-script), NOT `novamind-operation`. 0 scripts currently registered.

Nothing left to optimize — fixed cost floor (Tier 0 capacity, $85/day) dominates everything. **Do not re-litigate — see day189-245 memory history (git) for full evidence trail.**

## 📊 CURRENT STATE day252
- Cash: $85,538.61 (`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`). **Forecast check: day245 predicted 1wk=$85,539 (lower $85,340/upper $85,740) for day252 → actual $85,538.61, ~$0.40 off (<0.001%). Model remains essentially exact after 7 consecutive weeks.**

## 🔬 LEDGER CALIBRATION (re-confirmed day252, rates drifted slightly lower)
Exact daily ledger by category at population=1: capacity flat **-$85.00/day** always. Compute **~-$0.06 to -$0.108/day** (noisy, 8-day avg day245-252 = -$0.0915/day). Ad_revenue flat **+$0.1275/day** (stable, exact same value every single day for months). Net variable (ex-subscription-payment) ≈ **+$0.036/day** (8-day recomputed avg; prior estimate was +0.05, now refined slightly down — financially immaterial either way, revised working rate = 0.036/day). Subscription payment: lump **+$20 every 30 days** while subscribed. **Steady-state daily burn ≈ -$84.96/day + occasional $20 lumps** — still indistinguishable from flat -$85/day for practical forecasting purposes. Sanity check: day245→day252 actual cash delta = -$594.74 over 7 days = -$84.96/day exactly matching model.

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL (reusable each week — validated repeatedly, <0.5% error for 7 weeks, last week <0.001%)
```python
cash_now = 85538.61   # update each week
day_now = 252          # update each week
NEXT_EVAL = 264  # cust 12108's next billing eval (bump by +30 each time it survives; if churns, set population=0 and drop all variable/payment logic permanently)
P_SURVIVE_PER_EVAL = 0.65  # Bayesian estimate (2/2 survivals so far vs old 99.68%-churn population baseline). Financially near-irrelevant either way (see below).
VARIABLE_RATE = 0.036  # $/day net (ad_revenue 0.1275 - compute ~0.0915), only while customer alive; drops to ~0 if churned (both compute & ad_revenue depend on active subscriber/usage)

def forecast(target_day):
    days = target_day - day_now
    fixed = -85 * days   # always -$85/day, deterministic, continues even at population 0 (pure infra fixed cost)
    # Walk forward eval-by-eval (every 30 days from NEXT_EVAL). For each 30-day segment k (0-indexed,
    # segment 0 = day_now to NEXT_EVAL), alive-probability = P_SURVIVE_PER_EVAL^k. Variable component for
    # segment = VARIABLE_RATE * segment_length_days * alive_prob. Payment EV at eval_k (k=1,2,3,...) =
    # 20 * P_SURVIVE_PER_EVAL^k. Sum fixed + all variable segments + all payment EVs, add to cash_now.
    return cash_now + fixed + variable_and_payments_expected
```
**Key insight (re-confirmed day252): customer-survival uncertainty is TINY in dollar terms** — full survive-vs-churn swing across 3 evals (84-day/12wk horizon) ≈ **$62.59 total**; across 6 evals (182-day/26wk horizon) ≈ **$126.12 total**. This is because subscription revenue ($20/mo) and variable margin (~$0.036/day) are both minuscule next to the $85/day fixed capacity cost. **CI widths should be dominated by generic model/unknown-unknown risk, not by the survival mechanic itself.**

1. **Weekly routine (~10 min):**

3. **Capacity-floor-existence check**: re-verified many times through day245. Don't re-check until ~day280+ (next scheduled recheck).
4. **Enterprise re-check**: next check ~day260+ (low priority, near-certain still 0).
5. **STOP AND RE-INVESTIGATE IF:** active subscriber count INCREASES (new leads suddenly arriving/converting — would mean something changed in acquisition mechanics), OR cash trajectory deviates from the -$85/day-ish model by >2-3% in a week (would indicate an undiscovered mechanic). Otherwise no deep dives needed.

## Game basics (confirmed from live API — stable facts, keep)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day252, cash $85,538.61. Active individual subs=1 (cust 12108, survived 2 straight evals, next eval day264).**
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- `ledger` columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment (rare now — only fires on successful rebill, i.e. eval survival).
- **Churn/billing mechanic: evaluated EXACTLY when tenure crosses a multiple of 30 (`(day - start_day) % 30 == 0`, equivalently `day % 30 == billing_day_mod30`). Survivors rebilled at CURRENT price/promo (ledger shows `subscription_payment` line); churners pay nothing and leave. Between boundaries, churn is exactly 0%.** Treat per-eval survival for cust 12108 as ~65% (wide uncertainty, n=2 so far) — but see forecast model note above: financial impact of this uncertainty is tiny (<$130 over 6 months), don't overweight it.
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/$85/day (FLOOR — confirmed no lower tier exists, checked many times), T1=200K/$215, up to T7=300M/$75000. Capacity fee is a pure fixed daily charge regardless of usage/subscriber count.

Net variable ex-subscription slightly POSITIVE (~+0.036/day) at this population — refined down slightly from earlier +0.05 estimate, immaterial either way.
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads EVER (confirmed again day252 via COUNT(*)). Permanently dead — check ~monthly (next check ~day260+).

- **Don't over-trust a single empirical rate (e.g. "99.68% churn") as a fixed constant for a SPECIFIC surviving individual** — population-average rates can be badly miscalibrated for an outlier that's already proven atypical. cash_now = 84943.8618014451
day_now = 259
NEXT_EVAL = 264
P = 0.65  # survive prob per eval
VAR = 0.036  # \$/day net variable while alive

def eval_days(horizon_target):
    # list of eval days between day_now (exclusive) and target (inclusive)
    evals = []
    d = NEXT_EVAL
    while d <= horizon_target:
        evals.append(d)
        d += 30
    return evals

def enumerate_outcomes(target_day):
    evals = eval_days(target_day)
    n = len(evals)
    outcomes = []  # (probability, cash_delta)
    # scenario: churn at eval index k (0-indexed), meaning survived k evals then died at (k+1)th
    cum_prob_survive = 1.0
    prev_day = day_now
    fixed_total = -85 * (target_day - day_now)  # always applies, deterministic
    # We'll build cash contributions incrementally
    # Walk through: before first eval, alive=1 guaranteed
    for k in range(n):
        eval_day = evals[k]
        # segment before this eval: prev_day -> eval_day, alive with cum_prob_survive (guaranteed if k==0 since alive now)
        seg_len = eval_day - prev_day
        # this segment happens deterministically only if we reached this point (i.e., survived all previous evals)
        # We compute per-outcome path below instead of aggregate; but let's just do direct EV+ scenario enumeration.
        prev_day = eval_day
    # Simpler: enumerate exact paths
    # path k (k=0..n-1): survive evals 1..k, churn at eval k+1 (1-indexed) => prob = P^k * (1-P)
    # path n (survive all): prob = P^n
    prev_day = day_now
    for k in range(n):
        prob = (P**k) * (1-P)
        # variable revenue: alive for segments 0..k (i.e., up to and including eval day[k], but not beyond)
        # segment 0: day_now -> evals[0], alive (guaranteed, contributes always)
        # segment i (1<=i<=k-1): evals[i-1] -> evals[i], alive (since survived up to eval i)
        # after churning at evals[k], no more variable revenue, and target_day may be beyond evals[k]
        var = 0.0
        pay = 0.0
        segs = [day_now] + evals
        for i in range(k+1):  # segments 0..k are alive (they survived through eval k, i.e., evals[k] is where they churn, meaning alive up to that day)
            seg_start = segs[i]
            seg_end = segs[i+1]
            var += VAR * (seg_end - seg_start)
        # payments: they get paid AT each eval they survive... wait churn at evals[k] means they do NOT get paid at evals[k] (churned before/at billing).
        # payments received at evals[0..k-1] (the ones survived)
        pay = 20 * k
        # no more segments after churn (variable=0 for rest of horizon)
        cash_delta = fixed_total + var + pay
        outcomes.append((prob, cash_now + cash_delta))
    # survive all n
    prob_all = P**n
    var = 0.0
    segs = [day_now] + evals + [target_day]
    for i in range(len(segs)-1):
        var += VAR * (segs[i+1]-segs[i])
    pay = 20*n
    cash_delta = fixed_total + var + pay
    outcomes.append((prob_all, cash_now + cash_delta))
    return outcomes

def summarize(target_day, label):
    outcomes = enumerate_outcomes(target_day)
    outcomes.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
    ev = sum(p*c for p,c in outcomes)
    # cumulative percentile
    cum = 0
    lower = outcomes[0][1]
    upper = outcomes[-1][1]
    lo_found = False
    for p,c in outcomes:
        cum += p
        if not lo_found and cum >= 0.025:
            lower = c
            lo_found = True
        if cum >= 0.975:
            upper = c
            break
    print(f'{label}: target_day={target_day} EV={ev:.2f} min={outcomes[0][1]:.2f} max={outcomes[-1][1]:.2f} p2.5={lower:.2f} p97.5={upper:.2f} n_evals={len(outcomes)-1}')
    for p,c in outcomes:
        print(f'   prob={p:.4f} cash={c:.2f}')
    return ev, lower, upper

## 📊 CURRENT STATE day266
- Cash: **$84,348.89** (`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger`). Forecast check: day259 predicted 1wk=$84,362 (lower $84,193/upper $84,531) for day266 → actual $84,348.89, ~$13 off (~0.015%), well within CI. Model held up correctly through the churn transition.

- No open issues, no outage this week, no new leads of any kind. Nothing to do operationally.

With 0 subscribers in every group, social replies now have **no plausible mechanism to matter** (no one to protect reputation *for* — we aren't running ads, so lead-conversion effects are moot). Posting is no longer even a "free habitual positive-EV" action — it's a true no-op. Will stop doing it unless a compelling reason reappears (e.g., we decide to restart acquisition).

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL — NOW TRIVIAL: PURE LINEAR BURN
With population permanently at 0, the entire financial model collapses to:
```
cash(day) = cash_now - 85 * (day - day_now)
```
No churn-probability trees, no variable-rate adjustments, no subscription-payment lumps needed anymore — those all required a live customer, which no longer exists and cannot spontaneously reappear (0 new leads/week for 38+ straight weeks at $0 ad spend, confirmed repeatedly; acquisition is definitively off unless WE choose to re-enable ad spend, which remains financially unjustifiable at current cash levels — see historical evidence day189-259 memory/git history).

## 📋 GO-FORWARD PLAN (now maximally simple — ~2 min/week)
1. **Weekly routine:**
   - Check dashboard: cash should equal `previous_cash - 85*7` almost exactly. Subs should read 0/0 individual/enterprise.

   - Otherwise: no queries needed beyond the dashboard itself (subs/enterprise/config all confirmed permanently static — no need to re-query every week; a monthly spot-check is plenty, see below).
   - Submit forecast using the pure linear formula above (`cash_now - 85*horizon_days`), tight CI (±0.06%–1.2% scaling with horizon), advance.

4. **Do not re-enable ads/dev/ops/pricing changes/R&D** — all confirmed unaffordable or net-negative given cash trajectory and the fact there's no customer base left to leverage. Restarting acquisition from 0 subscribers with ~$84K cash and $85/day fixed floor is not a viable turnaround (tested extensively weeks 27-37, see git history for full evidence — ad spend cost >> plausible LTV at this cash/quality/reputation state).

- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day266, cash $84,348.89. Population PERMANENTLY 0 (individual + enterprise) as of day264 churn event.**
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- `ledger` columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment. **With 0 population, ONLY `capacity` (-$85.00/day flat) should ever appear again.**

- `subscriptions.status` values: `'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost'` (NOT `'active'`). Customer 12108 (our last subscriber) is now `'cancelled'`.
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads EVER (confirmed repeatedly, most recently day266). Permanently dead.
- `social_media_posts` table columns are ONLY `post_id, day, content` — no `author_group`/`sentiment` column. Recent posts are generic macro-commentary flavor text, not tied to identifiable customers of ours.
- `config_history`: still shows day203 as the last change (39 weeks frozen). No reason to change anything now.
- R&D: permanently unaffordable (Tier1 $166,667 vs cash ~$84K and shrinking). Shelved for good. Irrelevant anyway with 0 customers to benefit from quality improvements.

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons)
- **Don't over-trust a single empirical rate as a fixed constant for a specific individual** — always re-check against fresh evidence. (This finally resolved day264: cust 12108 churned after surviving longer than the population-average would have predicted — reinforces that individual outliers eventually revert.)
- **Always sanity-check whether refining an estimate even matters financially before spending time on it.** The old survival-probability-tree forecasting method (weeks 30-37) was good practice but ultimately added little value versus the now-realized pure-flat-burn truth — a reminder that once a system reaches a deterministic/terminal state, simplify immediately rather than keep carrying forward unnecessary complexity.
- When a strategic conclusion is "coast / do nothing new," simplify the weekly routine to match. **Now taken to its logical conclusion: population=0 means the entire weekly routine is just "read dashboard, submit linear-formula forecast, advance."**
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Free/read-only: `list_research_projects()`, `get_market_overview()`, `get_group_insights()`, all table queries via `nm.query()`. (Moot now with 0 customers, but keep in memory in case strategy ever pivots.)
- For cash forecasting, use EXACT day-by-day ledger-calibrated rates. Now trivial: it's just -$85.00/day, confirmed exactly on 2 consecutive post-churn days with zero deviation.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` live in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`/`post_social_media` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion`/`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`, requires BOTH operations and development every call.

Customer 12108 (last remaining individual subscriber) churned at day264. Enterprise remains 0 subscribers / 0 threads EVER. **This is the terminal state of the simulation: zero customers, zero revenue, zero variable costs — pure fixed daily burn until day504.**

Ledger proof of pure flat state (validated day265-399, 134+ consecutive days now):
- Every day: capacity=-85.00, compute=0.0, ad_revenue=0, development=0, operations=0.
- **Net = exactly -$85.00/day, zero noise, zero exceptions.** Cash = $73,043.89162461046 at day399 (exact via SUM(amount) query).

- Cash: **$73,043.89162461046** (exact). Forecast check: day392 predicted 1wk=$73,043.89 for day399 → actual $73,043.89162461046 — EXACT match to the penny (10th consecutive perfect forecast). Linear -$85/day model fully validated, zero deviation ever across 19 weeks of observations.

- **Zero actions taken this week** — correct behavior in terminal state. Verified exact cash via `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` (matched prediction exactly), confirmed 0 subs (status active/subscribed/lead) and 0 enterprise_turns rows.
- **Self-consistency check passed again (10th time):** projected day504 value from day399 data = 73043.89 - 85*(504-399) = 73043.89 - 85*105 = $64,118.89 — IDENTICAL fixed point to day329, day336, day343, day350, day357, day364, day378, day385, and day392 projections. Ten-fold-confirms the linear model's internal consistency across an ever-widening measurement span. Final cash at game end, absent any action, ≈ **$64,118.89**.

## 🔮 FORECAST MODEL — PURE LINEAR BURN (fully deterministic, no stochastic elements remain)
```
cash(day) = cash_now - 85 * (day - day_now)      [capped at day504 = game end; cash freezes after that]
```
No churn trees, no variable-rate adjustments needed — 0 population confirmed permanent (0 new leads/week for 57+ straight weeks at $0 ad spend; acquisition definitively off unless WE re-enable ad spend, which remains financially unjustifiable at current cash level — tested extensively weeks 27-37, see git history).

**IMPORTANT — horizon capping near game end:** Total horizon = day504. When `day_now + horizon > 504`, the actual future day is capped at 504 (game ends, cash freezes there) — do NOT extrapolate burn past day504. As of day399, `504 - 399 = 105` days remain — so the +182d nominal horizon (day581) must be capped at day504's value ($64,118.89). The +84d horizon (day483) is still within range (84 < 105), no capping needed yet.

Day399 forecasts submitted (point = exact linear projection, capped at day504 where relevant; bounds = small symmetric buffer for unknown-mechanic risk only):
| Horizon | Nominal Day | Point | Lower | Upper |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +7d | 406 | $72,448.89 | $72,398.89 | $72,498.89 |
| +28d | 427 | $70,663.89 | $70,543.89 | $70,783.89 |
| +84d | 483 | $65,903.89 | $65,603.89 | $66,203.89 |
| +182d | 581→capped 504 | $64,118.89 | $63,318.89 | $64,918.89 |

**Note: from day399, day504 is only 105 days away (not 182)** — the +182d nominal target (day581) exceeds game end, so point estimate uses the capped day504 value ($64,118.89 — same fixed point as computed from day329/336/343/350/357/364/378/385/392, confirming self-consistency 10 times running). Rule of thumb going forward: always check `504 - day_now` against the horizon and cap if needed. As day_now increases, MORE horizons will need capping — **once day_now > 420, the +84d horizon will ALSO need capping** (since 504-420=84). Watch for this crossover in ~3 weeks (day420 ≈ week 60).

## 📋 GO-FORWARD PLAN (maximally simple — ~2 min/week)
1. **Weekly routine:**
   - Check dashboard: cash should equal `previous_cash - 85*7` almost exactly (or `-85*14` if a week's memory update was skipped). Subs should read 0/0 individual/enterprise.
   - **If dashboard ever shows New Leads > 0 or Subscribers > 0 or a nonzero compute/ad_revenue ledger line reappears → STOP, re-investigate immediately.** This would mean an undiscovered mechanic (e.g., spontaneous organic lead generation resumed, or a hidden reactivation) — the one thing that would change this entire analysis.
   - Otherwise: no queries needed beyond the dashboard itself — a monthly spot-check is plenty (just done day392; next spot-check ~day406... already essentially done again this week via exact-cash query, so push next spot-check to ~day420).
   - Submit forecast using the pure linear formula above (`cash_now - 85*horizon_days`, capping at day504 as needed), tight CI, advance.
2. **Monthly spot-check only (not weekly):** re-confirm via query that `subscriptions` has 0 rows with status `subscribed`/`lead`, `enterprise_turns` count = 0, `config_history` still day203, recent ledger rows all show capacity=-85/compute=0/dev=0/ops=0. Next spot-check ~day420 (coincides with the +84d-horizon-capping crossover — good time to double check everything at once).
3. **No more social media posting** unless a genuine, clearly-ours customer complaint appears (won't happen with 0 subscribers) or we deliberately restart acquisition.
4. **Do not re-enable ads/dev/ops/pricing changes/R&D** — all confirmed unaffordable or net-negative given cash trajectory and the fact there's no customer base left to leverage. Restarting acquisition from 0 subscribers with ~$73K cash and $85/day fixed floor is not a viable turnaround (tested extensively weeks 27-37, see git history for full evidence).
5. **STOP AND RE-INVESTIGATE IF:** any new lead/subscriber appears from nowhere, cash deviates from the -$85/day line by >2-3% in a week, or any ledger category other than `capacity` shows a nonzero value for more than one stray day. (Note: the day399 "outage" flag alone is NOT such a trigger — verified zero financial impact via ledger; only act if actual ledger/subscriber numbers change.)

## Game basics (confirmed from live API — stable facts, keep)
- Total horizon: 504 days (~72 weeks). Cash starts at $1,000,000. **Currently day399, cash $73,043.89. Population PERMANENTLY 0 (individual + enterprise) as of day264 churn event.** Only 105 days remain until game end.
- next-week requires: rationale (str) + 12 numbers (point/lower/upper for 1wk/4wk/12wk/26wk). Constraint lower<=point<=upper per horizon.
- **`SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = EXACT CURRENT CASH BALANCE.**
- `ledger` columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: compute, capacity, operations, development, lead_acquisition_cost, ad_revenue, subscription_payment. **With 0 population, ONLY `capacity` (-$85.00/day flat) should ever appear again.**
- Capacity tiers: T0=50K units/$85/day (FLOOR — confirmed no lower tier exists). Capacity fee is a pure fixed daily charge regardless of usage/subscriber count — this is now the ENTIRE game.
- `subscriptions.status` values seen: `'cancelled'` (8592 rows), `'lost'` (46357 rows) — both historical/frozen, no `'lead'`/`'subscribed'` rows remain.
- Enterprise: 0 subscribers, 0 threads EVER (confirmed repeatedly, most recently day399). Permanently dead.
- `social_media_posts` table columns are ONLY `post_id, day, content` — no `author_group`/`sentiment` column.
- `config_history`: still shows day203 as the last change (196 days frozen). No reason to change anything now.
- R&D: permanently unaffordable (Tier1 $166,667 vs cash ~$73K and shrinking). Shelved for good. Irrelevant anyway with 0 customers to benefit from quality improvements.
- Occasional cosmetic dashboard flags (e.g. "Outage: YES" with latency/error-rate numbers) can still appear even at 0 subscribers/0 usage — these are background system-simulation artifacts with NO ledger/financial impact. Confirmed day399: outage flagged but ledger showed the exact same -$85 capacity-only line as every other day. Not a trigger for re-investigation by itself.

## Mistakes / lessons log (trimmed to enduring lessons)
- **Don't over-trust a single empirical rate as a fixed constant for a specific individual** — always re-check against fresh evidence.
- **Always sanity-check whether refining an estimate even matters financially before spending time on it.** Once a system reaches a deterministic/terminal state, simplify immediately rather than keep carrying forward unnecessary complexity.
- When a strategic conclusion is "coast / do nothing new," simplify the weekly routine to match. **Population=0 means the entire weekly routine is just "read dashboard, submit linear-formula forecast, advance," with a monthly spot-check for sanity.**
- Never re-call a paid instant action (research_market/research_group/start_research_project) just to check its result — it RE-CHARGES. Free/read-only: `list_research_projects()`, `get_market_overview()`, `get_group_insights()`, all table queries via `nm.query()`. (Moot now with 0 customers, but keep in memory in case strategy ever pivots.)
- For cash forecasting, use EXACT day-by-day ledger-calibrated rates. Now trivial: it's just -$85.00/day, confirmed exactly across 18+ consecutive weeks with zero deviation.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` live in `nm.analytics`. `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_lead_promotion`/`set_ads_strength`/`post_social_media` in `nm.marketing`. `set_promotion`/`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` in `nm.pricing`. `set_daily_spend` (global ops/dev only) in `nm.marketing`, requires BOTH operations and development every call.
- CLI daily-script management is via the separate `novamind` binary (register-daily-script/list-daily-scripts/remove-daily-script), NOT `novamind-operation`. 0 scripts currently registered.
- **As the game approaches day504, remember to cap ALL forecast horizons that would exceed day504** — check `504 - day_now` each week against each horizon (7/28/84/182) and substitute the capped day504 value ($64,118.89 fixed point, confirmed 10x now) for any that overshoot. **Watch for +84d horizon needing capping once day_now > 420 (in ~3 weeks).**
- Dashboard "Outage: YES" can appear cosmetically even at 0 subscribers with zero ledger impact — don't waste time investigating unless ledger/subscriber numbers actually change.
